_meta.description: Help tips (native-help.js). 'byName': a menu option by its name attribute (its path, e.g. /User/CallForwardingAlways/); a page's title uses the same entry for its page. 'bySection': a sidebar or menu board section by level (Reseller, ServiceProvider, Group, User: the first part of the level's menu paths) and then its name. 'bySetting': a setting on a page, by the page's path and then the setting's label as shown. Settings > Debug view outlines what has no entry yet and copies stubs in this shape.

/Reseller/ServiceProviders/?enterprise=f.title: Service Providers
/Reseller/ServiceProviders/?enterprise=f.body: A Service Provider is a top-level administrative container that groups and tenants live under. From here you add, modify, or remove service providers managed by this reseller. Service Providers are the non-enterprise model: groups under them are administered independently rather than sharing enterprise-wide settings. Use this when onboarding a new carrier customer that does not need shared enterprise dial plans or services.

/Reseller/ServiceProviders/?enterprise=t.title: Enterprises
/Reseller/ServiceProviders/?enterprise=t.body: An Enterprise is a Service Provider configured in 'enterprise mode', enabling features shared across all of its groups — enterprise-wide dial plans, voice VPN, common phone lists, and centralized administration. Add, modify, or remove enterprises here. Choose the Enterprise model (over a plain Service Provider) when a single organization has multiple groups/sites that should share numbering and services.

/Reseller/Groups/.title: Groups
/Reseller/Groups/.body: A Group is the site/location level where users, devices, and group services (Auto Attendant, Hunt Groups, Call Center, etc.) are provisioned. This screen lists all groups in the reseller across every service provider/enterprise, letting you search and jump into any group to manage its users and services.

/Reseller/Users/.title: Users
/Reseller/Users/.body: A User represents an individual subscriber — typically tied to a phone number, extension, and device. This screen displays all users in the reseller so you can locate a subscriber regardless of which group they belong to, then open their profile to manage assigned services, calling features, and credentials.

/Reseller/ServiceInstances/.title: Service Instances
/Reseller/ServiceInstances/.body: A Service Instance is a virtual subscriber — a service that behaves like a user but isn't a person: Auto Attendants, Hunt Groups, Call Centers, Meet-Me Conference bridges, Voice Messaging Groups, and similar. This screen lists all service instances in the reseller so you can find and manage these resources independently of human users.

/Reseller/Profile/.title: Profile
/Reseller/Profile/.body: The reseller Profile holds the reseller's own identifying information — name, contact details, address, and administrative metadata. Display or modify the reseller's profile here. This is configuration about the reseller entity itself, not about the groups or users beneath it.

/Reseller/Admins/.title: Administrators
/Reseller/Admins/.body: Reseller Administrators are the login accounts that can manage this reseller in CommPilot. Add, modify, or remove administrators and set their privilege level (full or restricted/read-only access to specific functions). Use this to control who can provision and change configuration at the reseller level.

/Reseller/DeviceActivationPolicy/.title: Activation Code Device Onboarding Policies
/Reseller/DeviceActivationPolicy/.body: Controls how phones/devices are securely onboarded using an Activation Code rather than manual MAC/credential entry. The policy defines whether activation codes are required, their length, and expiry. When enabled, a technician enters a short code on the phone to claim and provision it — reducing misconfiguration and improving security during deployment.

/Reseller/AlternateUserIDs/.title: Alternate User IDs
/Reseller/AlternateUserIDs/.body: An Alternate User ID is an additional login identifier a user can sign in with, besides their primary user ID (for example an email-style ID alongside the system ID). This screen lists all alternate user IDs in the reseller. Useful where users expect to authenticate with a familiar address instead of the BroadWorks-format user ID.

/Reseller/StirShaken/.title: STIR/SHAKEN
/Reseller/StirShaken/.body: STIR/SHAKEN is the caller-ID authentication framework that cryptographically signs outbound calls and verifies inbound ones to combat illegal spoofing and robocalls. Configure signing, attestation/tagging level (A/B/C), and verification behavior here. Correct configuration is often a regulatory requirement for delivering trusted caller ID.

/Reseller/CallRecordingPlatforms/.title: Call Recording Platforms
/Reseller/CallRecordingPlatforms/.body: A Call Recording Platform is an external recording system integrated with BroadWorks that captures and stores call audio. This screen lists the recording platforms available to the reseller; once defined, a platform can be assigned to users or groups whose Call Recording service routes its media there. Configure these when offering compliance or quality-monitoring recording.

/Reseller/Endpoints/.title: Identity/Device Endpoints
/Reseller/Endpoints/.body: An Identity/Device Endpoint is an individual line/port on a device profile — the registration that binds a user or service to a physical or soft phone. This screen lists all endpoints assigned across the reseller, so you can see which devices are in use and how lines are allocated.

/Reseller/DeviceType/.title: Identity/Device Profile Types
/Reseller/DeviceType/.body: An Identity/Device Profile Type is the template for a model of phone or device (for example a Polycom VVX, a Yealink, or a generic SIP endpoint). It defines the model's capabilities, number of ports, config-file handling, and tags. Add, modify, or remove the device types available in the reseller; individual device profiles are then created from these types.

/Reseller/DeviceInventory/.title: Identity/Device Profile Inventory
/Reseller/DeviceInventory/.body: The Identity/Device Profile Inventory lists every provisioned device profile — each an instance of a device type — across the reseller. These are the actual phones and devices configured for users and groups. Use it to find a specific device, see its assignment, and manage endpoints regardless of which group owns them.

/Reseller/Domains/.title: Domains
/Reseller/Domains/.body: A Domain is a SIP domain (the part after the @ in a user's address) available for assignment to groups and users. This screen lists all domains provisioned at the reseller; groups draw from these when creating users so each identity is addressed within an approved domain.

/Reseller/DnManagement/.title: Numbers
/Reseller/DnManagement/.body: Numbers are the telephone numbers (DNs) in the reseller's inventory, available to assign to groups, users, and services. This screen displays all phone numbers at the reseller level so you can see what is available, assigned, or activated, and manage number allocation across groups.

/Reseller/DnSummary/.title: Numbers Usage
/Reseller/DnSummary/.body: Numbers Usage is a reporting view of how the reseller's phone numbers are being consumed — totals and breakdowns of assigned versus available DNs across groups. Use it to gauge number-inventory utilization and plan when more numbers need to be ordered.

/Reseller/NumberRanges/.title: Enterprise Trunk Number Ranges
/Reseller/NumberRanges/.body: Enterprise Trunk Number Ranges define contiguous blocks of numbers carried over Enterprise Trunking — the trunk-based routing that lets an enterprise present many DIDs across shared trunk capacity. This screen lists the number ranges configured for the reseller's enterprise trunks.

/Reseller/NumberPrefixes/.title: Enterprise Trunk Number Prefixes
/Reseller/NumberPrefixes/.body: Enterprise Trunk Number Prefixes define the leading digit patterns used to route calls over Enterprise Trunks. This screen lists the prefixes provisioned for the reseller, which determine which dialed numbers are carried on enterprise trunk groups.

/Reseller/XsiPolicyProfile/ServiceProvid.title: Xsi Policy Profile
/Reseller/XsiPolicyProfile/ServiceProvid.body: An Xsi Policy Profile governs what the Xtended Services Interface (Xsi) APIs are allowed to do — the policy controlling third-party and client-application access to call control and user data over BroadWorks' web-services interface. This screen lists the Xsi policy profiles assigned at the reseller, used to authorize integrations such as Receptionist, Call Center, and UC clients.

/Reseller/DeviceFamilies/.title: Device Management Device Families
/Reseller/DeviceFamilies/.body: A Device Management Device Family groups related device types so configuration tag sets can be applied to many models at once. Add, modify, or remove device families, which are used to assign tag sets to one or more device types — simplifying Device Management configuration across a fleet.

/Reseller/DeviceTags/.title: Device Management Tag Sets
/Reseller/DeviceTags/.body: A Device Management Tag Set is a collection of configuration tags (name/value pairs) substituted into device config files during provisioning. Add, modify, or remove the tag sets assignable to device types, and manage the reseller's default tag set — this is how feature settings and parameters are pushed to phones through Device Management.

/Reseller/MSDNManagement/.title: Mobile Subscriber Directory Numbers
/Reseller/MSDNManagement/.body: Mobile Subscriber Directory Numbers (MSDNs) are the mobile numbers managed for BroadWorks Mobility — the directory numbers tied to mobile or SIM-based subscribers. This screen lists all MSDNs in the reseller, used when provisioning mobile lines and fixed-mobile convergence features.

/Reseller/CallNotify/.title: Call Notify
/Reseller/CallNotify/.body: Call Notify emails a designated address when an incoming call matches defined criteria, including the caller's number and name. This reseller-level screen manages Call Notify configuration and the email templates used, so the service can be offered consistently to the groups and users beneath the reseller.

/Reseller/Collaborate/.title: Collaborate
/Reseller/Collaborate/.body: Collaborate is BroadWorks' built-in audio and video conferencing service — meeting rooms, screen sharing, and instant or reservationless conferences. This reseller-level screen manages Collaborate configuration so the collaboration service can be authorized and provisioned for groups and users.

/Reseller/EmergencyZone/.title: Emergency Zones
/Reseller/EmergencyZone/.body: Emergency Zones define location-based boundaries that control where devices are permitted to register and how emergency (911) calls are handled, helping ensure calls route with the correct location. This reseller-level screen manages the emergency zone configuration applied to groups and users.

/Reseller/VM/.title: Voice Messaging
/Reseller/VM/.body: Voice Messaging is the voicemail service — mailboxes, greetings, and message delivery and notification. This reseller-level screen manages voice messaging configuration and defaults so voicemail can be authorized and applied to the groups and users beneath the reseller.

/Reseller/CallCenter/.title: Call Center
/Reseller/CallCenter/.body: Call Center is BroadWorks' ACD contact-center service — queues, agents, supervisors, and routing policies. This reseller-level screen is the entry point for Call Center configuration that supports the queues and agents provisioned within groups.

/Reseller/MeetMeConferencing/.title: Meet-Me Conferencing
/Reseller/MeetMeConferencing/.body: Meet-Me Conferencing provides dial-in audio conference bridges — conference ports with host and attendee access codes. This reseller-level screen is the entry point for Meet-Me Conferencing configuration that supports the bridges provisioned within groups.

/Reseller/EmergencyCallNotification/.title: Emergency Call Notification
/Reseller/EmergencyCallNotification/.body: Emergency Call Notification alerts designated people — by email or a monitoring group — whenever a 911 or emergency call is placed, supporting safety and compliance requirements such as Kari's Law. This reseller-level screen configures who is notified and how when an emergency call occurs.

/Reseller/MailParameters/.title: Mail Parameters
/Reseller/MailParameters/.body: Mail Parameters define the outbound email (SMTP) settings BroadWorks uses to send notifications — voicemail-to-email, Call Notify, fault alerts, and similar. This reseller-level screen configures the mail server, sender address, and related parameters so the platform's email features deliver correctly.

/ServiceProvider/Members/.title: Groups
/ServiceProvider/Members/.body: Lists every group in this service provider or enterprise, the site or location level where users, devices, and group services live. From here you can add a group, search the list, and open any group to manage it. Groups can only use the services and resources authorized at this level.

/ServiceProvider/Users/.title: Users
/ServiceProvider/Users/.body: Searches users across every group in this service provider or enterprise. Enter a name, user ID, phone number, or other detail to find a user and open their profile. Because each user belongs to a group, this is the quickest way to find someone when you do not know their group.

/ServiceProvider/ServiceInstances/.title: Service Instances
/ServiceProvider/ServiceInstances/.body: Lists the service instances, such as Auto Attendants, Hunt Groups, and Call Centers, set up in the groups under this service provider or enterprise. Use it to find an instance across all groups and open it for editing. Each instance still belongs to its own group and uses that group's numbers and resources.

/ServiceProvider/Profile/.title: Profile
/ServiceProvider/Profile/.body: Shows the basic details of this service provider or enterprise, such as its name, contact person, address, and support email. Admins at this level can review and update these details. Keeping them current helps other administrators and support staff identify the customer and reach the right contact.

/ServiceProvider/Admins/.title: Administrators
/ServiceProvider/Admins/.body: Lists the administrators who can manage this service provider or enterprise. Here you can add an administrator, change their details or password, or remove them. Administrators added at this level can typically work in every group beneath, while administrators for a single group are added within that group.

/ServiceProvider/Schedules/.title: Schedules
/ServiceProvider/Schedules/.body: Defines time schedules and holiday schedules at the service provider or enterprise level. Groups and users beneath can select these schedules in time-based services such as Auto Attendant business hours, so shared calendars like public holidays only need to be kept up to date in one place.

/ServiceProvider/DeviceActivationPolicy/.title: Activation Code Device Onboarding Policies
/ServiceProvider/DeviceActivationPolicy/.body: Controls how phones in this service provider or enterprise are onboarded with an activation code instead of manual MAC address or credential entry. The policy defines whether activation codes are used and how they behave for its devices. Check it before a rollout so installers know whether each phone will need a code.

/ServiceProvider/AlternateUserIDs/.title: Alternate User IDs
/ServiceProvider/AlternateUserIDs/.body: Lists the alternate user IDs set up for users in this service provider or enterprise. An alternate user ID is an extra identity a user can sign in with alongside their main user ID. Use this page to search for an alternate ID and see which user it belongs to.

/ServiceProvider/CallProcessingPolicy/.title: Call Processing Policies
/ServiceProvider/CallProcessingPolicy/.body: Sets call processing defaults for this service provider or enterprise, such as calling line ID rules, limits on simultaneous calls and call duration, and media options. Groups and users beneath follow these settings unless they are set to use their own policies. Change them here to affect every group that has not overridden them.

/ServiceProvider/DialPlanPolicy/.title: Dial Plan Policy
/ServiceProvider/DialPlanPolicy/.body: Defines the dial plan for this service provider or enterprise, including the public and private digit maps and access codes such as the code users dial for an outside line. Groups beneath can use these settings or switch to their own dial plan policy. Change it when the customer's dialing habits differ from the system default.

/ServiceProvider/RoutingProfile/.title: Routing Profile
/ServiceProvider/RoutingProfile/.body: Shows and sets the routing profile for this service provider or enterprise. A routing profile is defined at the system level and tells BroadWorks which network routing to apply to calls from this customer. Change it only when your network team asks, because it affects how this customer's calls are routed.

/ServiceProvider/DialableCallerID/.title: Dialable Caller ID
/ServiceProvider/DialableCallerID/.body: Configures Dialable Caller ID for this service provider or enterprise. The service adds prefix digits to the calling number of incoming calls, so users can return a call from their call log without editing the number. Here you define the matching criteria and prefix digits used for users beneath who have the service.

/ServiceProvider/StirShaken/.title: STIR-SHAKEN
/ServiceProvider/StirShaken/.body: Controls STIR/SHAKEN caller ID authentication for this service provider or enterprise. STIR/SHAKEN signs outgoing calls and checks incoming ones, so the network can show whether a calling number has been verified. Settings here control how signing and verification apply to calls for the groups beneath.

/ServiceProvider/Carriers/.title: Carriers
/ServiceProvider/Carriers/.body: Sets the preferred carriers for this service provider or enterprise for intra-LATA, inter-LATA, and international calls. Carriers are defined at the system level and chosen here from that list. Groups and users with the Preferred Carrier service can use these choices or pick their own.

/ServiceProvider/GroupPagingTargetsCapac.title: Group Paging Targets Capacity
/ServiceProvider/GroupPagingTargetsCapac.body: Sets the limit on how many paging targets Group Paging instances can have in this service provider or enterprise. Each group can set its own capacity, but not above the value set here. Raise it when a customer needs larger paging groups than the current limit allows.

/ServiceProvider/Endpoints/.title: Identity/Device Endpoints
/ServiceProvider/Endpoints/.body: Lists the endpoints across this service provider or enterprise, showing which users and service instances use which identity/device profiles and line/ports. Use it to find where a device or line/port is in use, for example before replacing or removing a phone.

/ServiceProvider/DeviceInventory/.title: Identity/Device Profiles
/ServiceProvider/DeviceInventory/.body: Manages identity/device profiles, the records for phones and other devices, at the service provider or enterprise level. Profiles created here can be used by any group beneath, unlike group-level profiles, which only their own group can use. Use this page to add, search, or modify devices and their settings.

/ServiceProvider/Domains/.title: Domains
/ServiceProvider/Domains/.body: Lists the domains assigned to this service provider or enterprise, including its default domain. A domain is the part of a user ID or line/port after the @ sign. Groups beneath can only use domains from this list, which is filled from the system's domains.

/ServiceProvider/NetworkClassesOfService.title: Network Classes of Service
/ServiceProvider/NetworkClassesOfService.body: Shows the Network Classes of Service (NCOS) assigned to this service provider or enterprise, including the default. An NCOS decides which calls are allowed and how they are routed in the network. Groups and users beneath can only be given classes from this list, which is set on Assign Network Classes of Service.

/ServiceProvider/DnManagement/.title: Numbers
/ServiceProvider/DnManagement/.body: Lists the phone numbers held by this service provider or enterprise and shows which are assigned to groups and which are still free. Numbers pass from here to groups, where they are given to users and services. Adding new numbers at this level is normally done by a system or reseller administrator.

/ServiceProvider/NumberRanges/.title: Enterprise Trunk Number Ranges
/ServiceProvider/NumberRanges/.body: Lists the number ranges set up for Enterprise Trunks in this enterprise. Calls to a number within a range can be routed to an enterprise trunk without that number being assigned to a trunk user, which suits PBX sites with large number blocks. The ranges come from numbers the enterprise already holds.

/ServiceProvider/NumberPrefixes/.title: Enterprise Trunk Number Prefixes
/ServiceProvider/NumberPrefixes/.body: Lists the number prefixes set up for Enterprise Trunks in this enterprise. Calls to any number that starts with one of these prefixes can be routed to an enterprise trunk, which suits PBX sites handling large number blocks. It works alongside Enterprise Trunk Number Ranges, which match numbers between a start and end number instead.

/ServiceProvider/OfficeZones/.title: Office Zones
/ServiceProvider/OfficeZones/.body: Defines office zones for this service provider or enterprise. An office zone groups one or more zones, set up at the system level, to describe where a group's users are allowed to work from. Office zones are used by Zone Calling Restrictions to limit what users can do when they are outside that area.

/ServiceProvider/RoutePointExternalSyste.title: Route Point External Systems
/ServiceProvider/RoutePointExternalSyste.body: Lists the external systems available to Route Point service instances in this service provider or enterprise. A Route Point hands calls to an outside application, such as a third-party contact center, for distribution, and the external system identifies that application. Systems appear here once a higher-level administrator has assigned them.

/Operator/ServiceProviders/AuthorizeServ.title: Services
/Operator/ServiceProviders/AuthorizeServ.body: Authorizes which group and user services this service provider or enterprise may use, and sets how many of each can be assigned. Only services authorized here can be passed down to groups and then to users. Changes are normally made by a system or reseller administrator when the customer's service offering changes.

/ServiceProvider/ServicePacks/.title: Service Packs
/ServiceProvider/ServicePacks/.body: Creates and manages service packs for this service provider or enterprise. A service pack bundles several user services under one name so they can be assigned to a user in one step. Packs can only contain services authorized here, and each pack has its own limit on how many can be assigned.

/ServiceProvider/ServicePackUtilization/.title: Service Pack Usage
/ServiceProvider/ServicePackUtilization/.body: Shows how service packs are used across this service provider or enterprise, including which groups have users assigned to each pack. Use it to check how close a pack is to its limit before adding users, or to find which groups rely on a pack before changing or retiring it.

/ServiceProvider/SACCapacity/.title: Session Admission Control Capacity
/ServiceProvider/SACCapacity/.body: Sets how many concurrent sessions, meaning calls in progress, this service provider or enterprise may have under Session Admission Control. The value here acts as a ceiling for the limits set in the groups beneath. When a limit is reached, new calls are blocked until others end.

/ServiceProvider/SystemDefinedCriteria/.title: System Defined Communication Barring Criteria
/ServiceProvider/SystemDefinedCriteria/.body: Lists the outgoing Communication Barring criteria defined at the system level that this service provider or enterprise can use. Each criterion describes a type of outgoing call, such as international or premium-rate calls. Use them in Communication Barring profiles, alongside your own digit pattern criteria, to decide which calls are allowed or blocked.

/ServiceProvider/SystemDefinedIncomingCr.title: System Defined Communication Barring Incoming Criteria
/ServiceProvider/SystemDefinedIncomingCr.body: Lists the incoming Communication Barring criteria defined at the system level that this service provider or enterprise can use. Each criterion describes a type of incoming call. Use them in Communication Barring profiles to control which incoming calls the users beneath can receive, alongside the outgoing criteria on the neighboring page.

/ServiceProvider/TrunkingCallCapacity/.title: Trunking Call Capacity
/ServiceProvider/TrunkingCallCapacity/.body: Sets the maximum number of simultaneous trunking calls for this service provider or enterprise, along with any bursting capacity above that. The capacity is shared out to the groups beneath for their trunk groups, and group allocations cannot exceed the totals set here.

/ServiceProvider/XsiPolicyProfile/Group/.title: Xsi Policy Profile
/ServiceProvider/XsiPolicyProfile/Group/.body: Sets which Xsi policy profile applies to groups in this service provider or enterprise. Xsi is the interface that clients and integrations use to control calls and services, and a policy profile limits what they can do through it. The profiles to choose from are defined at the system level.

/Operator/ServiceProviders/AssignDomains.title: Assign Domains
/Operator/ServiceProviders/AssignDomains.body: Assigns domains from the system's list to this service provider or enterprise. Only assigned domains can be used for its groups, users, and line/ports, so add a domain here before trying to use it further down. This page is normally managed by a system or reseller administrator.

/ServiceProvider/AssignNetworkClassesOfS.title: Assign Network Classes of Service
/ServiceProvider/AssignNetworkClassesOfS.body: Assigns Network Classes of Service (NCOS) from the system's list to this service provider or enterprise and sets which one is the default. Only assigned classes can be given to its groups and users. This is normally done by a system or reseller administrator when setting up a customer.

/ServiceProvider/AssignRoutePointExterna.title: Assign Route Point External Systems
/ServiceProvider/AssignRoutePointExterna.body: Assigns route point external systems from the system's list to this service provider or enterprise. Once assigned, a system can be selected by Route Point service instances in its groups. This is normally done by a system or reseller administrator when a customer starts using an outside call distribution application.

/ServiceProvider/AssignXsiPolicyProfile/.title: Assign Xsi Policy Profile
/ServiceProvider/AssignXsiPolicyProfile/.body: Assigns an Xsi policy profile from the system's list to this service provider or enterprise. An Xsi policy profile limits what clients and integrations can do through Xsi, the interface they use to control calls and services. This is normally managed by a system or reseller administrator when setting up a customer.

/ServiceProvider/IMRNsManagement/.title: IMRNs
/ServiceProvider/IMRNsManagement/.body: Manages the IMRNs (IP Multimedia Routing Numbers) available to this service provider or enterprise. IMRNs are temporary routing numbers used to bring calls from mobile phones into BroadWorks, mainly for BroadWorks Mobility. They come from a pool assigned by a higher-level administrator and are used automatically, not given to individual users.

/ServiceProvider/MSDNManagement/.title: Mobile Subscriber Directory Numbers
/ServiceProvider/MSDNManagement/.body: Lists the mobile subscriber directory numbers (MSDNs) held by this service provider or enterprise for BroadWorks Mobility. These are the numbers of users' mobile phones, and they are passed down to groups and assigned to mobility users there. They are managed separately from the ordinary numbers on the Numbers page.

/ServiceProvider/ExternalCustomRingback/.title: External Custom Ringback
/ServiceProvider/ExternalCustomRingback/.body: Configures External Custom Ringback for this service provider or enterprise. The service plays callers a custom ringback, such as music or a message, from an external media server instead of the standard ringing tone. Settings here tell BroadWorks whether and how to use that server for calls to the groups and users beneath.

/ServiceProvider/ICSA/.title: In-Call Service Activation
/ServiceProvider/ICSA/.body: Sets up In-Call Service Activation for this service provider or enterprise. It lets users start services such as call transfer during a call by dialing a digit sequence, which helps on phones without a transfer key. The activation digits set here apply to users beneath who have the service.

/ServiceProvider/IntegratedIMP/.title: Integrated IM&P
/ServiceProvider/IntegratedIMP/.body: Sets up Integrated IM&P (instant messaging and presence) for this service provider or enterprise. It links users' BroadWorks accounts to the messaging and presence service used by their clients, so they can chat and see each other's status. Settings here, such as the domain used for IM&P addresses, apply to the groups and users beneath.

/ServiceProvider/VM/.title: Voice Messaging
/ServiceProvider/VM/.body: Sets voice messaging options for this service provider or enterprise, such as the email addresses that message deliveries and notifications are sent from. You can keep the system defaults or enter addresses that match the customer's own domain. The settings apply to Voice Messaging users in the groups beneath.

/ServiceProvider/VP/.title: Voice Portal
/ServiceProvider/VP/.body: Sets Voice Portal options for this service provider or enterprise. The Voice Portal is the phone menu users call to check voice messages and change greetings and call settings. For an enterprise, this is where you choose whether the portal works across all groups or only within each group.

/ServiceProvider/AdviceOfCharge/.title: Advice Of Charge
/ServiceProvider/AdviceOfCharge/.body: Sets up Advice of Charge for this service provider or enterprise. The service shows users call charge information on their phones, during or at the end of a call, based on charging data from the network. Settings here apply to users beneath who have the service assigned.

/ServiceProvider/BroadWorksMobility/.title: BroadWorks Mobility
/ServiceProvider/BroadWorksMobility/.body: Sets BroadWorks Mobility options for this service provider or enterprise. BroadWorks Mobility ties a user's mobile phone to their BroadWorks identity, so calls and services work the same on the mobile as on the desk phone. Here you choose whether to follow the system's settings or use your own for the groups and users beneath.

/ServiceProvider/MWIMobile/.title: MWI Delivery to Mobile Endpoint
/ServiceProvider/MWIMobile/.body: Configures MWI Delivery to Mobile Endpoint for this service provider or enterprise. It sends message waiting indications, which tell users they have new voice mail, to their mobile phones. Settings here, such as whether the service is enabled, apply to users beneath who have the service.

/ServiceProvider/NumberPortabilityQuery/.title: Number Portability Query
/ServiceProvider/NumberPortabilityQuery/.body: Configures number portability queries for this service provider or enterprise. When enabled, BroadWorks checks whether a dialed number has been ported to another carrier before routing the call, so it reaches the right network. Settings here apply to calls from the groups beneath.

/ServiceProvider/SACWhiteList/.title: Session Admission Control Allow List
/ServiceProvider/SACWhiteList/.body: Lists the numbers or digit patterns that are exempt from Session Admission Control in this service provider or enterprise. Calls to these destinations can still go through when a session limit has been reached. Use it for essential numbers, such as emergency or support lines, that must never be blocked by a capacity limit.

/ServiceProvider/ThirdPartyEmergency/.title: Third-Party Emergency Calling
/ServiceProvider/ThirdPartyEmergency/.body: Sets up Third-Party Emergency Calling for this service provider or enterprise. It sends emergency calls to an outside emergency calling provider, which routes them to the right emergency center with the caller's location. Settings here, such as whether the service is enabled, apply to the groups and users beneath.

/ServiceProvider/ZoneCallingRestrictions.title: Zone Calling Restrictions
/ServiceProvider/ZoneCallingRestrictions.body: Sets up Zone Calling Restrictions for this service provider or enterprise. The service uses office zones to restrict what users can do when their device is outside their permitted area, such as making calls or registering. Use it together with Office Zones, which define the permitted areas.

/ServiceProvider/CommBarring/DigitPatter.title: Digit Pattern Criteria
/ServiceProvider/CommBarring/DigitPatter.body: Defines digit pattern criteria for Communication Barring in this service provider or enterprise. Each criterion is a named list of digit patterns, such as number prefixes, that describes a type of call. Use these criteria in Communication Barring profiles to allow or block calls that match.

/ServiceProvider/CommBarring/Profiles/.title: Profiles
/ServiceProvider/CommBarring/Profiles/.body: Creates and manages Communication Barring profiles for this service provider or enterprise. A profile combines criteria with actions, such as allow or block, to decide which calls users can make or receive. Profiles defined here are assigned to groups beneath, which then apply them to their users.

/ServiceProvider/MeetMeConference/.title: Meet-Me Conference Ports
/ServiceProvider/MeetMeConference/.body: Shows the Meet-Me Conferencing ports allocated to this service provider or enterprise. Each port lets one participant join a conference, so the total limits how many people can be in conferences at the same time. Ports given to the groups beneath come out of this total.

/ServiceProvider/BWAnywhereNumberLookup/.title: BroadWorks Anywhere Number Lookup
/ServiceProvider/BWAnywhereNumberLookup/.body: Searches the BroadWorks Anywhere locations of users in this service provider or enterprise for a phone number. BroadWorks Anywhere lets calls to a user's business number also ring other phones, such as a mobile or home phone. Use this page to find which user has a given outside number set up as a location.

/Common/DeviceProfileAuthPasswordRules/?.title: Device Profile Authentication Password Rules
/Common/DeviceProfileAuthPasswordRules/?.body: Sets the rules for device profile authentication passwords in this service provider or enterprise, such as minimum length and required characters. These passwords let phones sign in to the Device Management System to download their configuration files. The rules apply when these passwords are set or changed for devices beneath.

/ServiceProvider/EmergencyCallNotificati.title: Emergency Call Notification
/ServiceProvider/EmergencyCallNotificati.body: Sets up email notification of emergency calls for this service provider or enterprise. When a user places an emergency call, BroadWorks can send an email to the address set here, for example to alert reception or on-site security. Use it where someone on site needs to know quickly that an emergency call was made.

/ServiceProvider/FAC/.title: Feature Access Codes
/ServiceProvider/FAC/.body: Shows and changes the feature access codes used in this service provider or enterprise, the star codes users dial to control services such as call forwarding. You can change a code or add an alternate code to match what users are used to. Codes set here apply to the groups beneath unless a group sets its own.

/Common/Password_Rules/?UserLevel=Servic.title: Password Rules
/Common/Password_Rules/?UserLevel=Servic.body: Sets the web portal password rules for administrators and users in this service provider or enterprise, such as minimum length, required characters, and expiry. You can keep the system's rules or define your own. The rules apply whenever passwords are created or changed for accounts beneath this level.

/Common/PasscodeRules/?UserLevel=Service.title: Passcode Rules
/Common/PasscodeRules/?UserLevel=Service.body: Sets the passcode rules for this service provider or enterprise, such as minimum length, disallowed digit patterns, and lockout after failed attempts. Passcodes are the numeric codes users enter on the phone to reach the Voice Portal and their voice messages. The rules apply to users in the groups beneath.

/Common/SipAuthPasswordRules/?UserLevel=.title: SIP Authentication Password Rules
/Common/SipAuthPasswordRules/?UserLevel=.body: Sets the rules for SIP authentication passwords in this service provider or enterprise, such as minimum length and required characters. SIP authentication passwords are what phones and soft clients use to register with BroadWorks. The rules apply when these passwords are set or changed for users and trunk groups beneath.

/ServiceProvider/AnswerConfirmation/.title: Answer Confirmation
/ServiceProvider/AnswerConfirmation/.body: Sets up the announcement used for answer confirmation in this service provider or enterprise. When answer confirmation is required, a user answering on another phone, such as a mobile reached through BroadWorks Anywhere, must press a key to accept the call, which stops a voice mail system from answering it. Here you choose the default or a custom announcement.

/ServiceProvider/DefaultConfig/.title: Device Configuration
/ServiceProvider/DefaultConfig/.body: Lists the device types whose configuration files can be customized for this service provider or enterprise. You can review the files a device type uses and upload your own versions for this customer. Changes affect devices of that type in the groups beneath, unless a group or device has its own customization.

/ServiceProvider/DMEventQueues/.title: Device Management Event Queues
/ServiceProvider/DMEventQueues/.body: Shows the Device Management events queued for this service provider or enterprise, such as requests to rebuild device configuration files or reset phones. Use it to check whether changes have been processed, and to see pending, in-progress, or completed events after a bulk update.

/ServiceProvider/ServicePackMigration/.title: Service Pack Migration
/ServiceProvider/ServicePackMigration/.body: Moves users from one set of services or service packs to another in bulk, across groups in this service provider or enterprise. You create a migration task, choose the groups and users it covers, and schedule when it runs. Use it when changing service offerings, such as retiring an old service pack.

/ServiceProvider/VPBranding/.title: Voice Portal Branding
/ServiceProvider/VPBranding/.body: Uploads custom greetings for the Voice Portal in this service provider or enterprise, such as the main greeting users hear when they reach it. Branding set here applies to the groups beneath unless a group uploads its own. Use it to give a customer's Voice Portal its own announcements instead of the system defaults.

/Operator/System/System_Preferences/?sp=.title: Web Portal Branding
/Operator/System/System_Preferences/?sp=.body: Customizes how the CommPilot web portal looks for this service provider or enterprise, such as the logo and other branding its administrators and users see. Branding set here is used in place of the system branding for this customer's portal pages. It is normally managed by a system or reseller administrator.

/Group/Members/.title: Users
/Group/Members/.body: Lists every user in the group and lets you search for a user, open one to manage, or add a new user. Opening a user takes you to the User level, where you manage that user's profile, phone number, device, and calling services.

/Group/Profile/.title: Profile
/Group/Profile/.body: Shows the group's basic details and lets you update them, such as its name, contact details, address, time zone, default domain, and calling line ID name and number. The group calling line ID can be presented on users' outgoing calls, depending on the group's Call Processing Policies.

/Group/Admins/.title: Administrators
/Group/Admins/.body: Lists the administrators who can log in to CommPilot and manage this group, and lets you add, edit, or remove them. A group administrator only has access to this group, and what each one can change is set by that administrator's own policies.

/Group/AnnouncementRepository/Audio/.title: Announcement Repository
/Group/AnnouncementRepository/Audio/.body: Stores the audio and video announcement files uploaded for this group, such as greetings and hold music. Files kept here can be selected in group services like Auto Attendant and Music/Video on Hold, so one upload can be reused across services.

/Group/Departments/.title: Departments
/Group/Departments/.body: Creates and manages departments within the group, used to organize users and group services into sections such as Sales or Support. Departments can be nested, and a department administrator can be limited to managing only the users in their own department.

/Group/Schedules/.title: Schedules
/Group/Schedules/.body: Defines the group's time schedules and holiday schedules, such as business hours or public holidays. Group schedules can then be selected by services in the group, for example Auto Attendant business hours and holiday menus, or the criteria of users' selective call features.

/Group/DeviceActivationPolicy/.title: Activation Code Device Onboarding Policies
/Group/DeviceActivationPolicy/.body: Controls how phones in this group can be onboarded using an activation code rather than manual MAC address or credential entry. Use it when rolling out devices that support activation codes, so a technician can claim and provision each phone by entering a short code on it.

/Group/AlternateUserIDs/.title: Alternate User IDs
/Group/AlternateUserIDs/.body: Lists the alternate user IDs defined for users in this group. An alternate user ID is an extra identifier for an existing user, kept alongside the primary user ID, and this page helps you see which user an alternate ID belongs to.

/Group/CallProcessingPolicy/.title: Call Processing Policies
/Group/CallProcessingPolicy/.body: Sets call handling rules for the group, such as which calling line ID is presented on outgoing calls, limits on simultaneous calls and call duration, and media policy. The group can follow the service provider's settings or use its own, and users can in turn have their own policies.

/Group/CommBarringAuthCodes/.title: Communication Barring Authorization Codes
/Group/CommBarringAuthCodes/.body: Lists the authorization codes that let callers in this group get past a Communication Barring restriction. When a barring rule requires authorization, the caller is prompted for a code, and a valid code from this list lets the call through.

/Group/DialPlanPolicy/.title: Dial Plan Policy
/Group/DialPlanPolicy/.body: Defines how dialed digits are interpreted for the group, including access codes for reaching an outside line, whether an access code is required for public calls, and the public and private digit maps. It applies to every user in the group unless a user has custom dial plan settings.

/Group/Policies/.title: Group Web Policies
/Group/Policies/.body: Sets the web access policies for this group, which control what users can view or change for themselves in CommPilot, such as their profile, authentication settings, and the group directory. Permissions for individual administrators are set separately under Administrators.

/Group/RoutingProfile/.title: Routing Profile
/Group/RoutingProfile/.body: Selects the routing profile used for this group's calls. Routing profiles let calls from different groups be routed differently in the network, and they are created at system level, so you choose from the existing ones here.

/Group/VirtualOnNet/.title: Virtual On-Net Enterprise Extensions
/Group/VirtualOnNet/.body: Defines virtual on-net users: people outside BroadWorks, such as users on another PBX, who are given a name and extension so enterprise users can reach them by short dialing. Calls to them are treated as on-net calls, even though they are routed to an external number.

/Group/DialableCallerID/.title: Dialable Caller ID
/Group/DialableCallerID/.body: Converts the calling number shown on incoming calls into a format users can dial back directly, by adding prefix digits according to the matching criteria set here. It works together with the Dialable Caller ID option in Call Processing Policies.

/Group/StirShaken/.title: STIR-SHAKEN
/Group/StirShaken/.body: Sets how STIR/SHAKEN caller ID authentication applies to this group, including whether outgoing calls are signed with an attestation and how verification results on incoming calls are handled. Use it when the group needs settings different from those at the higher levels.

/Group/CallRecordingPlatform/.title: Call Recording Platform
/Group/CallRecordingPlatform/.body: Selects which call recording platform this group's calls are recorded on, from the platforms set up at system level. It applies to users in the group who are assigned a Call Recording service.

/Group/GroupPagingTargetsCapacity/.title: Group Paging Targets Capacity
/Group/GroupPagingTargetsCapacity/.body: Shows the maximum number of target users that can be added to each Group Paging group in this group. The value is set within the limit allowed by the service provider, so a paging group that needs more targets may need a higher-level change.

/Group/Endpoints/.title: Identity/Device Endpoints
/Group/Endpoints/.body: Lists every line/port on the group's identity/device profiles and the user or service each one is assigned to. Use it to see which devices are in use, or to find which device a given user or service is assigned to.

/Group/DeviceInventory/.title: Identity/Device Profiles
/Group/DeviceInventory/.body: Lists the identity/device profiles, such as phones and gateways, created in this group and lets you add, search for, or modify them. A profile holds the device type, MAC address, and authentication details, and its line/ports are then assigned to users or group services.

/Group/Domains/.title: Domains
/Group/Domains/.body: Lists the domains assigned to this group, which are used in user IDs, line/ports, and other addresses. Domains come from the service provider's list and are added to the group with Assign Domains, while the group's default domain is set on its Profile.

/Group/NetworkClassesOfService/.title: Network Classes of Service
/Group/NetworkClassesOfService/.body: Lists the network classes of service available to this group and shows which one is the default. A network class of service is defined at system level and sets network-level calling rules, such as call restrictions and routing, for the calls it applies to.

/Group/GroupDnManagement/.title: Numbers
/Group/GroupDnManagement/.body: Lists the phone numbers assigned to this group and shows which user or service each one is assigned to, and which are still free. Numbers reach the group from the service provider through Assign Numbers, and are then given to users or group services.

/Group/NumberRangesUsage/.title: Enterprise Trunk Number Ranges
/Group/NumberRangesUsage/.body: Shows the number ranges assigned to this group for enterprise trunks and whether each range is in use. A range lets calls to a block of numbers be routed through an enterprise trunk without a user for each number; ranges are added with Assign Enterprise Trunk Number Ranges.

/Group/NumberPrefixesUsage/.title: Enterprise Trunk Number Prefixes
/Group/NumberPrefixesUsage/.body: Shows the number prefixes assigned to this group for enterprise trunks and whether each one is in use. A prefix lets calls to numbers that start with it be routed through an enterprise trunk; prefixes are added with Assign Enterprise Trunk Number Prefixes.

/Group/OfficeZones/.title: Office Zones
/Group/OfficeZones/.body: Lists the office zones available to this group and which one is the default. An office zone is a set of network zones, defined at system level, that Location-Based Calling Restrictions uses to control which calls a user can make depending on where they are connected.

/Group/RoutePointExternalSystems/.title: Route Point External Systems
/Group/RoutePointExternalSystems/.body: Lists the route point external systems available to this group. These are external applications, defined at system level, that can be linked to the group's Route Point services; they are added to the group with Assign Route Point External Systems.

/ServiceProvider/Members/AuthorizeServic.title: Services
/ServiceProvider/Members/AuthorizeServic.body: Shows which user services, group services, and service packs are authorized for this group, and in what quantity. A service has to be authorized here before it can be assigned to users or to the group, and a service provider administrator can change these authorizations.

/Group/TrunkingCallCapacity/.title: Trunking Call Capacity
/Group/TrunkingCallCapacity/.body: Sets how many trunking calls this group can carry at once, within the capacity granted by the service provider. The limit is shared by all trunk groups in the group, and each trunk group's own capacity is set on that trunk group.

/Group/SACCapacity/.title: Session Admission Control Capacity
/Group/SACCapacity/.body: Sets the maximum number of concurrent sessions allowed for the group under Session Admission Control, with separate limits possible for originating and terminating calls. It helps keep the group from overloading its access network, for example a site's link with limited bandwidth.

/Group/XsiPolicyProfile/.title: Xsi Policy Profile
/Group/XsiPolicyProfile/.body: Shows the Xsi policy profile that applies to this group. Xsi policy profiles are defined at system level and set limits for applications that connect through the Xsi (Xtended Services Interface); the assignment is changed with Assign Xsi Policy Profile.

/ServiceProvider/Members/AssignDomains/.title: Assign Domains
/ServiceProvider/Members/AssignDomains/.body: Adds domains from the service provider's list to this group, or removes them, so they can be used in the group's user IDs and line/ports. Use it before creating users or devices whose addresses need a domain the group does not have yet.

/Group/AssignNetworkClassesOfService/.title: Assign Network Classes of Service
/Group/AssignNetworkClassesOfService/.body: Assigns network classes of service from the service provider's list to this group, or removes them. Classes assigned here become available to the group and appear on the Network Classes of Service page.

/Group/DnManagement/.title: Assign Numbers
/Group/DnManagement/.body: Moves phone numbers from the service provider's pool into this group, or returns unused ones. Numbers must be assigned to the group before they can be given to users or group services, and on some systems they also need to be activated.

/Group/NumberRangesAssign/.title: Assign Enterprise Trunk Number Ranges
/Group/NumberRangesAssign/.body: Assigns number ranges from the service provider to this group for use with enterprise trunks, or removes them. Once assigned, a range can be linked to an enterprise trunk so calls to numbers in it are routed through that trunk.

/Group/NumberPrefixesAssign/.title: Assign Enterprise Trunk Number Prefixes
/Group/NumberPrefixesAssign/.body: Assigns number prefixes from the service provider to this group for use with enterprise trunks, or removes them. Once assigned, a prefix can be linked to an enterprise trunk so calls to numbers starting with it are routed through that trunk.

/Group/AssignOfficeZones/.title: Assign Office Zones
/Group/AssignOfficeZones/.body: Assigns office zones from the service provider's list to this group, or removes them. Office zones are used by Location-Based Calling Restrictions to decide which calls a user can make based on where they are connected.

/Group/AssignRoutePointExternalSystems/.title: Assign Route Point External Systems
/Group/AssignRoutePointExternalSystems/.body: Assigns route point external systems from the service provider's list to this group, or removes them. A system must be assigned here before the group's Route Point services can be linked to it.

/Group/DnActivation/.title: Activate Numbers
/Group/DnActivation/.body: Activates or deactivates the phone numbers assigned to this group. On systems that use number activation, a number can be provisioned in advance and only goes live once it is activated, which helps when numbers are being ported in.

/Group/Services/.title: Assign Group Services
/Group/Services/.body: Assigns group services, such as Auto Attendant, Hunt Group, Call Park, or Music/Video on Hold, to this group from those authorized by the service provider. A group service must be assigned here before it can be set up under the Services menu.

/Group/AssignXsiPolicyProfile/Group/.title: Assign Xsi Policy Profile
/Group/AssignXsiPolicyProfile/Group/.body: Chooses which Xsi policy profile applies to this group, from the profiles available to it. Use it when applications that connect to the group through the Xsi interface need different limits from the default profile.

/Group/UserServices/.title: New User Services Template
/Group/UserServices/.body: Chooses the user services and service packs that are assigned automatically to every new user created in this group. It saves assigning the same services one user at a time; existing users are not changed, so use Existing User Services for them.

/Group/ExistingUserServices/.title: Existing User Services
/Group/ExistingUserServices/.body: Assigns or unassigns user services and service packs across the group's existing users in one step. Use it for bulk changes, such as giving every user a new service; users created later get their services from the New User Services Template instead.

/Group/IMRNsManagement/.title: IMRNs
/Group/IMRNsManagement/.body: Lists the IMRNs (IP Multimedia Routing Numbers) assigned to this group. IMRNs are routing numbers used to route calls from the mobile network into BroadWorks, and they are normally only needed when mobility services are deployed.

/Group/MSDNManagement/.title: Mobile Subscriber Directory Numbers
/Group/MSDNManagement/.body: Lists the mobile subscriber directory numbers assigned to this group. These are the mobile phone numbers used with BroadWorks Mobility, where each one can be assigned to a user as their mobile identity.

/Group/Auto_Attendant/.title: Auto Attendant
/Group/Auto_Attendant/.body: Lists the group's auto attendants and is where a new auto attendant is created. An auto attendant answers calls with a greeting and a menu so callers can reach users by pressing keys or dialing by name or extension, with separate business hours and after hours menus.

/Group/CallPark/.title: Call Park
/Group/CallPark/.body: Sets up Call Park for the group, which lets a user put a call on hold so another user can retrieve it from a different phone. Here you create call park groups, choose which users belong to each, and set group-wide options such as the recall timer.

/Group/CPU/.title: Call Pickup
/Group/CPU/.body: Creates and manages call pickup groups, whose members can answer a call ringing on another member's phone by dialing a feature access code. A user can belong to only one call pickup group at a time.

/Group/ExchangeIntegration/.title: Exchange Integration
/Group/ExchangeIntegration/.body: Holds the group's settings for connecting BroadWorks to a Microsoft Exchange server. It is used so that users' voice messages can be integrated with their Exchange mailboxes, and it only affects users whose voice messaging is set up to use it.

/Group/Hunt_Group/.title: Hunt Group
/Group/Hunt_Group/.body: Lists the group's hunt groups and is where a new hunt group is created. A hunt group has its own number and extension and distributes incoming calls to a list of agents using a policy such as circular, regular, simultaneous, uniform, or weighted.

/Group/IntegratedIMP/.title: Integrated IM&P
/Group/IntegratedIMP/.body: Shows the group-level settings for Integrated IM&P, the service that provides instant messaging and presence to users of BroadWorks clients. The service also has to be assigned to each user who needs it.

/Group/MusicOnHold/.title: Music/Video on Hold
/Group/MusicOnHold/.body: Sets the music or video callers hear or see when a call in this group is placed on hold or parked, using the system default or a custom file. Departments can have their own settings, and users with the user-level service can override the group choice.

/Group/Voice_XML/.title: VoiceXML
/Group/Voice_XML/.body: Lists the group's VoiceXML instances and is where a new one is created. A VoiceXML instance has its own number and passes calls to a VoiceXML application, for example to run a custom voice menu that the standard group services do not cover.

/Group/PreAlertingAnnouncement/.title: Pre-alerting Announcement
/Group/PreAlertingAnnouncement/.body: Sets an announcement that callers hear before an incoming call to the group is presented, such as a notice that calls may be recorded. Use it when the same message should play for calls to the group as a whole rather than setting it user by user.

/Group/Voice_Mail_Retrieval/General/.title: Voice Messaging
/Group/Voice_Mail_Retrieval/General/.body: Holds the group-wide settings for voice messaging, such as whether it is enabled for the group and which mail server stores and delivers messages. Each user's own mailbox options, like greetings and forwarding messages to email, are set on the user's Voice Management page.

/Group/VoicePortal/.title: Voice Portal
/Group/VoicePortal/.body: Configures the group's voice portal, the number users call to check voicemail, record greetings, and change settings by phone. Here you set its phone number, extension, name, and related options, which apply to all users in the group.

/Group/AdviceOfCharge/.title: Advice Of Charge
/Group/AdviceOfCharge/.body: Holds the group-level settings for Advice of Charge, which sends call charging information to users' phones during or at the end of a call. It applies to users in the group who are assigned the Advice of Charge service.

/Group/BroadWorksAnywhere/.title: BroadWorks Anywhere
/Group/BroadWorksAnywhere/.body: BroadWorks Anywhere lets users make and receive business calls from any phone, such as a mobile or home line, as if they were at their desk. At the group level you create and manage BroadWorks Anywhere portals, numbers users dial to place calls with their BroadWorks services. Each user's own locations are set on the user's pages.

/Group/BroadWorksMobility/.title: BroadWorks Mobility
/Group/BroadWorksMobility/.body: BroadWorks Mobility links users' mobile phones to BroadWorks so calls on the mobile network get the same business services as a desk phone. At the group level this page holds Mobility settings that apply across the group. Each user's mobile number and ringing options are configured on that user's Mobility page.

/Group/Call_Capacity/.title: Call Capacity
/Group/Call_Capacity/.body: Call Capacity limits how many calls a set of users in the group can have active at the same time. You create call capacity groups, add users to them, and set the maximum number of active, incoming, and outgoing calls for each. It is useful when a site's connection can only carry a limited number of calls.

/Group/CustomRingback/.title: Custom Ringback Group
/Group/CustomRingback/.body: Custom Ringback Group replaces the standard ringing that callers hear with a custom audio or video file when they call users in the group. On this page you choose or upload the ringback media for the group. Users with the Custom Ringback User service can set their own ringback on their user pages.

/Group/EmergencyZones/.title: Emergency Zones
/Group/EmergencyZones/.body: Emergency Zones defines the IP address ranges where the group's devices are expected to be, so emergency calls come from a known location. You enter the home zone's IP ranges and choose whether devices outside it are blocked from registering or only from making emergency calls. An email notification can also be turned on.

/Group/EnterpriseTrunk/.title: Enterprise Trunk
/Group/EnterpriseTrunk/.body: An Enterprise Trunk groups several trunk groups into one routing target, so calls can be spread across them and rerouted if one is unavailable. At the group level you build enterprise trunks from the group's own trunk groups and choose how calls are distributed among them. Create the trunk groups first on the Trunk Group page.

/Group/FindMeFollowMe/.title: Find-me/Follow-me
/Group/FindMeFollowMe/.body: Find-me/Follow-me is a group service with its own number that tries to reach someone by ringing a series of alerting groups, one after another. Each alerting group can ring several phone numbers or users at once. This page is where you create and manage the group's Find-me/Follow-me instances.

/Group/FlexibleSeatingHost/.title: Flexible Seating Host
/Group/FlexibleSeatingHost/.body: Flexible Seating Host is used for shared desks: the host holds the shared phone, and users with the Flexible Seating Guest service can sign in to it and use it as their own. This page is where you create the group's hosts. It works much like Hoteling, but the host is a group service rather than a user.

/Group/GroupNightForwarding/.title: Group Night Forwarding
/Group/GroupNightForwarding/.body: Group Night Forwarding forwards incoming calls for the group's users outside business hours or on holidays. You can turn it on manually or have it follow the business hours and holiday schedules you select. Use it when a whole site closes at night, instead of changing each user's forwarding one by one.

/Group/GroupPaging/.title: Group Paging
/Group/GroupPaging/.body: Group Paging lets a caller make a one-way announcement to a set of phones at once by dialing the paging group's number or extension. On this page you create paging groups and choose which users can send pages and which users' phones receive them. Unlike Instant Group Call, listeners cannot talk back.

/Group/InstantGroupCall/.title: Instant Group Call
/Group/InstantGroupCall/.body: Instant Group Call is a group service with its own number that calls a preset list of destinations at the same time and joins everyone who answers into one call. On this page you create instances and set their destination lists. Unlike Group Paging, the call is two-way, so everyone who answers can speak.

/Group/MWIMobile/.title: MWI Delivery to Mobile Endpoint
/Group/MWIMobile/.body: MWI Delivery to Mobile Endpoint sends message waiting notifications to a user's mobile phone, so they know a new voice message is waiting while away from the desk. At the group level this page holds the group's settings for the service. Users must have the service assigned to receive these notifications.

/Group/PolycomPhoneServices/.title: Polycom Phone Services
/Group/PolycomPhoneServices/.body: Polycom Phone Services connects supported Polycom phones to BroadWorks directories, so users can browse contacts from the phone's directory. At the group level you choose which group directory content, such as a Custom Contact Directory, is offered to the phones. Each user's own directory options are set on their Polycom Phone Services page.

/Group/PreferredCarrierGroup/.title: Preferred Carrier Group
/Group/PreferredCarrierGroup/.body: Preferred Carrier Group sets the long-distance carriers used for the group's calls: intraLATA, interLATA, and international. You can use the service provider's carriers or pick specific ones for the group. Users with the Preferred Carrier User service can have their own carriers set on their user pages.

/Group/RoutePoint/.title: Route Point
/Group/RoutePoint/.body: A Route Point is a group service that queues incoming calls while an external application, such as a contact center system, decides where to send them. On this page you create and configure Route Point instances, including their numbers, queue, and announcement settings. It is used when call routing is controlled outside BroadWorks rather than by a Call Center.

/Group/SeriesComplete/.title: Series Completion
/Group/SeriesComplete/.body: Series Completion links users in an ordered list so that a call to a busy member moves on to the next member in the series. On this page you create series completion groups and set their members and order. Unlike a Hunt Group, it has no number of its own; it only handles calls made to its members.

/Group/SACGroup/.title: Session Admission Control Group
/Group/SACGroup/.body: Session Admission Control Group limits how many calls a set of devices can have at the same time, usually to protect a site's network bandwidth. You create SAC groups, add the devices that share the limit, and set the maximum number of sessions, with separate originating and terminating limits. Call Capacity is the similar limit for users rather than devices.

/Group/ExternalVoiceMail/.title: Third-Party Voice Mail Support
/Group/ExternalVoiceMail/.body: Third-Party Voice Mail Support sends calls to a voice mail system outside BroadWorks when a user is busy or doesn't answer. At the group level you enter the external voice mail server's number and set the group's redirect defaults. Users with the service can use this group server or have their own server number.

/Group/TrunkGroup/.title: Trunk Group
/Group/TrunkGroup/.body: A Trunk Group connects a customer's PBX or other SIP equipment to BroadWorks so its users can make and receive calls through the trunk. At the group level you create trunk groups, choose the access device, set the maximum number of active calls, and assign a pilot user. Trunk groups can be combined into an Enterprise Trunk for routing.

/Group/AccountCodes/General/.title: Administration
/Group/AccountCodes/General/.body: Administration holds the group's Account/Authorization Codes settings: which of the two code types the group uses, how many digits a code has, and which users it applies to. Account codes tag outgoing calls for billing or tracking, while authorization codes must be valid before a call is allowed. The codes themselves are added under Codes Management.

/Group/AccountCodes/CodesMgmt/.title: Codes Management
/Group/AccountCodes/CodesMgmt/.body: Codes Management is where you add, edit, and delete the group's individual account or authorization codes, each with an optional description. Users enter one of these codes when placing a call that requires it. The code type and length are set on the Administration page in this section.

/Group/Call_Center/.title: Call Centers
/Group/Call_Center/.body: Call Centers lists the group's call center instances, each with its own number, queue, and agents. This is where you create a call center, choose its type (Basic, Standard, or Premium), and open it to manage agents, routing, and announcements. The options shown depend on the call center type and the services assigned to the group.

/Group/Call_Center/DefaultProperties/?us.title: Agent Default Settings
/Group/Call_Center/DefaultProperties/?us.body: Agent Default Settings holds the group's default settings for call center and route point agents. Agents use these values unless their own call center settings are changed, which saves setting the same options for each agent. Check here first when many agents in the group behave the same unexpected way.

/Group/Call_Center/ThresholdsProfiles/.title: Agent Threshold Profiles
/Group/Call_Center/ThresholdsProfiles/.body: Agent Threshold Profiles set time limits for agent activity, such as time on a call, in wrap-up, or unavailable, after which the agent's status is flagged as a warning. Each agent is assigned one profile, and supervisors see the alerts in their call center client. Use it to spot agents who may need help.

/Group/Call_Center/UnavailableCodes/.title: Agent Unavailable Codes
/Group/Call_Center/UnavailableCodes/.body: Agent Unavailable Codes are reason codes that call center agents pick when they set themselves to Unavailable, such as lunch or training. Here you turn the feature on, create and manage the codes, and choose default codes used automatically in certain cases, such as after bounced calls. The codes appear in call center reports.

/Group/CallCenterMonitoring/.title: Call Center Monitoring
/Group/CallCenterMonitoring/.body: Call Center Monitoring holds group-wide settings for how supervisors monitor the group's call centers. Changes here apply to every call center in the group. Which supervisors can monitor which agents is set separately in each call center's supervisor settings.

/Group/Call_Center/DispositionCodes/.title: Call Disposition Codes
/Group/Call_Center/DispositionCodes/.body: Call Disposition Codes let agents tag a call with its outcome or purpose, such as a sale or a complaint. Codes created here at the group level can be used by the group's call centers, and each call center can also have codes of its own. The codes are included in call center reports.

/Group/Call_Center/RoutingPriority/.title: Routing Priority Settings
/Group/Call_Center/RoutingPriority/.body: Routing Priority Settings decide which call an agent is offered first when the agent belongs to more than one of the group's call centers. You can offer the call that has waited longest, or rank the call centers so calls from higher-priority ones are offered first. It affects every agent who is in several call centers.

/Group/Call_Center/ExternalReporting/.title: External Reporting Settings
/Group/Call_Center/ExternalReporting/.body: External Reporting Settings control whether the group's call center activity is sent to an external reporting server, for reports produced outside BroadWorks. You choose the reporting server the group uses. Use it when the customer relies on a separate reporting or workforce management system.

/Group/ReportBranding/.title: Report Branding
/Group/ReportBranding/.body: Report Branding sets the logo or header shown on the group's call center reports. You can keep the default branding or upload a custom image for this group. It changes only how reports look, not the data they contain.

/Group/ReportTemplates/.title: Report Templates
/Group/ReportTemplates/.body: Report Templates lists the call center report templates available to the group, each defining what a report shows, such as agent activity or queue statistics. Here you review the templates and manage any the group adds. Scheduled and on-demand call center reports are built from these templates.

/Group/CCScheduledReports/.title: Scheduled Reports
/Group/CCScheduledReports/.body: Scheduled Reports lets you set up call center reports that run automatically on a schedule and are emailed to chosen recipients. Each schedule picks a report template, the call centers or agents to include, the time range, and how often it runs. Use it for regular reports so supervisors don't need to run them by hand.

/Group/Calling_Plan/CodesMgmt/.title: Codes Management
/Group/Calling_Plan/CodesMgmt/.body: Codes Management holds the authorization codes used by the Outgoing Calling Plan. When a call type or number is set to require an authorization code, the caller must enter one of these codes before the call goes through. These codes are separate from those in the Acct/Auth Codes section.

/Group/Calling_Plan/DigitStrings/.title: Digit Strings
/Group/Calling_Plan/DigitStrings/.body: Digit Strings is where you define the number patterns used by the Outgoing Digit Plan, such as a specific area code or prefix. After a string is added here, the Outgoing Digit Plan can allow, block, or otherwise restrict calls that match it. Use it when a call type is too broad and you need to control specific numbers.

/Group/Calling_Plan/PinholeDigitStrings/.title: Pinhole Digit Strings
/Group/Calling_Plan/PinholeDigitStrings/.body: Pinhole Digit Strings are number patterns that can be let through even when the Outgoing Calling Plan blocks their call type, such as a single toll number. You define the strings here and then set how each is handled on the Outgoing Pinhole Digit Plan page. They act as exceptions to the calling plan.

/Group/Calling_Plan/TransferNumbers/.title: Transfer Numbers
/Group/Calling_Plan/TransferNumbers/.body: Transfer Numbers are destinations, such as an operator or receptionist, that the Outgoing Calling Plan can send restricted calls to instead of simply blocking them. You set the group's transfer numbers here. Each call type or digit string in the outgoing plans can then be set to transfer to one of them.

/Group/Calling_Plan/Incoming/.title: Incoming Calling Plan
/Group/Calling_Plan/Incoming/.body: Incoming Calling Plan controls which types of incoming calls the group's users can receive, such as calls from outside the group or collect calls. The settings here are the group default and apply to every user who doesn't have a custom plan. A user's plan can be changed on that user's own Incoming Calling Plan page.

/Group/Calling_Plan/Outgoing/?isEnh=true.title: Outgoing Calling Plan
/Group/Calling_Plan/Outgoing/?isEnh=true.body: Outgoing Calling Plan controls which types of outgoing calls the group's users can make, such as local, toll, international, or premium-rate calls. For each call type you can allow it, block it, require an authorization code, or transfer it to a set number. These are group defaults that apply to users without a custom plan.

/Group/Calling_Plan/OutgoingDigitPlan/?i.title: Outgoing Digit Plan
/Group/Calling_Plan/OutgoingDigitPlan/?i.body: Outgoing Digit Plan applies calling plan rules to specific number patterns rather than broad call types. For each string defined under Digit Strings, you choose whether calls to it are allowed, blocked, need an authorization code, or go to a transfer number. These group settings apply to users without a custom digit plan.

/Group/Calling_Plan/OutgoingPinholeDigit.title: Outgoing Pinhole Digit Plan
/Group/Calling_Plan/OutgoingPinholeDigit.body: Outgoing Pinhole Digit Plan sets how calls to each pinhole digit string are handled, letting chosen numbers through even when the Outgoing Calling Plan blocks their call type. For each string you can ignore it, allow the call, or apply options such as requiring an authorization code. Define the strings first under Pinhole Digit Strings.

/Group/CommBarring/Profiles/.title: Profiles
/Group/CommBarring/Profiles/.body: Communication Barring profiles are sets of rules that allow, block, or redirect calls based on call type or number, and are an alternative to calling plans. At the group level this page shows the profiles available to the group and which one it uses by default. The profiles themselves are created at the service provider level.

/Group/MeetMeConferencePorts/.title: Meet-Me Conference Ports
/Group/MeetMeConferencePorts/.body: Meet-Me Conference Ports shows the conference ports allocated to the group for Meet-Me Conferencing, where each port lets one participant take part in a conference. The ports come from the service provider's allocation and are shared by the group's bridges. Check it when participants cannot join because the group has run out of ports.

/Group/ConferenceBridges/.title: Meet-Me Conference Bridges
/Group/ConferenceBridges/.body: Meet-Me Conference Bridges lists the group's conference bridges, each a group service with its own number that participants dial to join a meeting. Here you create bridges, set how many of the group's conference ports each can use, and choose which users can host conferences on it. Hosts then schedule their own conferences.

/Group/BWAnywhereNumberLookup/.title: BroadWorks Anywhere Number Lookup
/Group/BWAnywhereNumberLookup/.body: BroadWorks Anywhere Number Lookup finds which user in the group has a given phone number set up as a BroadWorks Anywhere location. Enter the number to see whose location it is. It is useful for tracing where an unfamiliar mobile or home number is configured.

/Group/PhoneList/.title: Common Phone List
/Group/PhoneList/.body: Common Phone List is a shared list of names and external phone numbers that every user in the group can see and dial from. You add entries one by one or import them from a file. It suits contacts everyone at the site calls, such as suppliers, while each user keeps a Personal Phone List of their own.

/Group/CustomContactDir/.title: Custom Contact Directories
/Group/CustomContactDir/.body: Custom Contact Directories let you build named directories that contain a chosen subset of the group's users and group services, rather than the whole Group Directory. Each directory can then be made available to phones or clients, for example through Polycom Phone Services. Use them when a site needs a shorter or departmental list.

/Group/EmergencyCallNotification/.title: Emergency Call Notification
/Group/EmergencyCallNotification/.body: Emergency Call Notification sends an email when someone in the group dials an emergency number. On this page you turn the notification on and enter the email address that should receive it. It helps site staff learn quickly that an emergency call has been made so they can respond.

/Group/Feature_Codes17/.title: Feature Access Codes
/Group/Feature_Codes17/.body: Feature Access Codes are the star codes users dial from their phones to use services, for example to turn call forwarding on or off. This page shows the codes available to the group and lets you change them or add alternate codes if the group needs to differ from the defaults. Changes affect every user in the group.

/Group/CompanyDir/.title: Group Directory
/Group/CompanyDir/.body: Group Directory lists everyone in the group, including users and group services such as Hunt Groups and Auto Attendants, with their phone numbers and extensions. You can search the list and open a printable version. It is a quick way to see who has which number or extension.

/Group/InventoryReport/.title: Inventory Report
/Group/InventoryReport/.body: Inventory Report builds a report of what is provisioned in the group, such as users, phone numbers, devices, and assigned services. You choose what to include and enter an email address, and the report is sent there. It is useful for audits or for checking a site's setup before or after changes.

/Common/Password_Rules/?UserLevel=Group.title: Password Rules
/Common/Password_Rules/?UserLevel=Group.body: Password Rules covers the requirements for web portal passwords in the group, such as minimum length, required character types, expiry, and lockout after failed attempts. Depending on your access, these rules may be set by the service provider and only viewable here. Voice portal passcodes are controlled separately under Passcode Rules.

/Common/PasscodeRules/?UserLevel=Group.title: Passcode Rules
/Common/PasscodeRules/?UserLevel=Group.body: Passcode Rules sets the requirements for the numeric passcodes users enter to reach the voice portal and voice mail by phone, such as length, blocked patterns like repeated digits, and expiry. The group can follow the higher-level rules or use its own. Web portal passwords are controlled separately under Password Rules.

/Group/DefaultConfig/.title: Device Configuration
/Group/DefaultConfig/.body: Device Configuration manages the group-level configuration files that Device Management uses to set up phones of each device type.
