You can view or upload custom files for a device type, and rebuild files or reset phones so changes take effect. Files set here apply to the group's devices of that type unless a device has its own file.

/Group/DMEventQueues/.title: Device Management Event Queues
/Group/DMEventQueues/.body: Device Management Event Queues shows device management tasks for the group, such as configuration file rebuilds and phone resets, and whether each is pending, in progress, or finished. Check it when phones don't pick up a change, to confirm that the rebuild or reset you started has completed.

/Group/ExtensionMgmt/.title: Extension Dialing
/Group/ExtensionMgmt/.body: Extension Dialing sets the length of extensions in the group, with a minimum, maximum, and default number of digits. Users dial these extensions to reach each other without the full phone number. Set it before adding users where possible, since new extensions must fit within these lengths.

/Intercept/?id=group.title: Intercept Group
/Intercept/?id=group.body: Intercept Group stops calls to and from the whole group and plays an announcement instead, for example when service is suspended or a site has moved. You can intercept incoming calls, outgoing calls, or both, and can tell callers a new number. It affects every user in the group, unlike Intercept User, which covers one user.

/Group/VPBranding/.title: Voice Portal Branding
/Group/VPBranding/.body: Voice Portal Branding replaces the standard greetings on the group's voice portal with your own recordings. You can upload custom audio for the voice portal greeting and the voice messaging greeting, or keep the defaults. It suits customers who want their company name in the prompts callers and users hear.

/User/Profile/.title: Profile
/User/Profile/.body: Holds the user's basic details: first and last name, the calling line ID name presented on the user's calls, department, language, time zone and contact details such as email. The time zone matters for schedule-based services, since the user's schedules are applied in that time zone.

/User/Addresses/.title: Addresses
/User/Addresses/.body: Sets the user's phone number and extension, and links the user to a phone by choosing an identity/device profile and line/port. Only numbers already assigned to the group can be selected, so a new number has to be added at group level before it can be given to the user.

/User/AnnouncementRepository/Audio/.title: Announcement Repository
/User/AnnouncementRepository/Audio/.body: Stores the audio and video announcement files uploaded for this user or virtual user, such as custom greetings, ringback or Auto Attendant menu prompts. Files kept here can be selected on any of the user's service pages that play a custom announcement, instead of uploading the same file again for each service.

/User/Password/.title: Passwords
/User/Password/.body: Changes the password the user signs in to the web portal with, and the passcode used for the voice portal and voice mail by phone. New values must meet the password and passcode rules set for the group or service provider, and resetting them here is the usual fix when a user is locked out.

/User/Schedules/.title: Schedules
/User/Schedules/.body: Lists the time and holiday schedules defined for this user alone, such as business hours or a vacation period. Criteria-based services like Call Forwarding Selective, Selective Acceptance and Selective Rejection can then act only during a chosen schedule, and group-level schedules are also available to them.

/User/DirectRoute/.title: Direct Route
/User/DirectRoute/.body: Configures Direct Route for this user, which ties the user to one or more trunk group identities so calls between BroadWorks and a connected PBX can be routed by that identity. It applies only to trunking setups, so leave it unchanged unless the customer's PBX integration requires it.

/User/RouteList/.title: Route List
/User/RouteList/.body: Assigns ranges of the group's phone numbers to this user so calls to any number in those ranges are delivered to the user, typically a trunk user serving a PBX. Settings here also control whether calls from the PBX may present a number from those ranges as the calling identity.

/User/AlternateUserIDs/.title: Alternate User IDs
/User/AlternateUserIDs/.body: Adds extra user IDs for this user besides the primary one, so the user can sign in to the web portal and supported clients with a different ID. Each alternate ID must be unique across the system, just like the primary user ID, and signs in to the same user account.

/User/Services/.title: Assign Services
/User/Services/.body: Assigns or removes individual user services and service packs for this user or virtual user. A service only appears in the user's menus once it is assigned here, and only services and packs authorized for the group, with licenses available, can be selected.

/User/AssignCallCenters/.title: Assign Call Centers
/User/AssignCallCenters/.body: Shows which call centers this user belongs to as an agent and whether the user is joined to each one. A joined agent is offered queued calls only while the agent's ACD state is Available, and agents usually change that state from their phone or desktop client.

/User/AgentSupervisors/.title: Assign Route Point Supervisors
/User/AgentSupervisors/.body: Sets which supervisors oversee this user's work as a Route Point agent. Route Point is the call queuing service used with an external routing application, so this page matters only for customers using it; supervisors for regular Call Center queues are set on each call center.

/User/AssignXsiPolicyProfile/.title: Assign Xsi Policy Profile
/User/AssignXsiPolicyProfile/.body: Assigns the Xsi policy profile that governs what this user's applications can do through Xsi, the BroadWorks interface that desktop clients and integrations use to monitor and control calls. Profiles are defined at a higher level, so change the assignment only when a client or integration needs different access.

/User/OCICAppPolicies/.title: Call Application Policies
/User/OCICAppPolicies/.body: Controls which call control applications connected through the BroadWorks Open Client Interface may monitor or control this user's calls. It matters only when the customer uses such an application, for example a CTI or attendant console integration, and otherwise has no effect on the user's calls.

/User/CallPolicies/.title: Call Policies
/User/CallPolicies/.body: Sets which calling line ID the recipient sees when the user's calls are redirected, for example by forwarding: the original caller's ID or the user's own. Showing the user's ID tells the recipient the call came through the user, while the original ID shows who is really calling.

/User/CallProcessingPolicy/.title: Call Processing Policies
/User/CallProcessingPolicy/.body: Overrides the group's call processing settings for this user only, such as the calling line ID presented on outgoing calls and limits like the maximum number of simultaneous calls. Leave it on the group setting unless one user must behave differently, since values set here take precedence over the group's.

/User/CommBarringAuthCodes/.title: Communication Barring Authorization Codes
/User/CommBarringAuthCodes/.body: Manages the authorization codes this user can enter to place calls that the Communication Barring profile marks as needing authorization, such as international calls. The user is only asked for a code when a barring rule's action requires authorization; calls that a rule simply blocks cannot be released with a code.

/User/DevicePolicies/.title: Device Policies
/User/DevicePolicies/.body: Controls how the user's phones work with BroadWorks, including the line mode and whether device feature synchronization keeps settings like Do Not Disturb and forwarding in step between the phone and BroadWorks. Synchronization only works with phones that support it, so confirm the phone model before turning it on.

/User/Privacy/.title: Privacy
/User/Privacy/.body: Hides the user from the group directory and from Auto Attendant dialing by name or extension, and can limit which users may monitor the user's phone status. With phone status privacy on, only the users listed here can watch the user's line through services such as Busy Lamp Field.

/User/OfficeZone/.title: Office Zone
/User/OfficeZone/.body: Assigns the user to an office zone, the set of network locations that BroadWorks treats as the user's office. It works with Location-Based Calling Restrictions, which can limit the calls the user places from a device outside that zone.

/User/ACR/.title: Anonymous Rejection - Off
/User/ACR/.body: Rejects calls from callers who have blocked their caller ID, playing them an announcement that the user does not accept anonymous calls. The call never rings the user, so a caller who wants to get through has to unblock their number and call again.

/User/CLIO/.title: Calling Line ID Blocking Override - Off
/User/CLIO/.body: Lets the user see the caller's number and name even when the caller has blocked their caller ID. It is intended for users with a genuine need to identify every caller, such as emergency or security staff, and it affects only calls the user receives.

/User/CallingNameDelivery/.title: Calling Name Delivery - On
/User/CallingNameDelivery/.body: Shows the caller's name on the user's phone for incoming calls, when a name is available. Delivery for external and internal callers can be switched on separately on this page, and callers who block their identity are still withheld.

/User/CNAM/.title: Calling Name Retrieval - Off
/User/CNAM/.body: Looks up the caller's name in an external calling name database for incoming calls, so the user sees a name even when the call arrives with only a number. It only works where the system has been set up with a name retrieval service, and blocked callers are not revealed.

/User/CallingNumberDelivery/.title: Calling Number Delivery - On
/User/CallingNumberDelivery/.body: Shows the caller's phone number on the user's phone for incoming calls. Delivery for external and internal callers can be switched on separately on this page, and callers who block their identity are still withheld from the user.

/User/CF/Always/.title: Call Forwarding Always - Off
/User/CF/Always/.body: Sends every incoming call to another number without ringing the user's phone. While it is on, Busy, No Answer and Not Reachable forwarding do not come into play, and an optional ring reminder plays a short ring on the phone so the user knows a call was forwarded.

/User/CF/AlwaysSecondary/.title: Call Forwarding Always Secondary - Off
/User/CF/AlwaysSecondary/.body: A second, independent Call Forwarding Always with its own destination, so all incoming calls can be sent to an alternate number without changing the main Call Forwarding Always settings. While on, it forwards calls without ringing the user's phone, so check both services when calls go somewhere unexpected.

/User/CF/Busy/.title: Call Forwarding Busy - Off
/User/CF/Busy/.body: Forwards incoming calls to another number when the user is already on a call and cannot take another, for example when Call Waiting is off. It is often pointed at a colleague or mobile, and when it is on it takes precedence over sending busy calls to voice mail.

/User/CF/No_Answer/.title: Call Forwarding No Answer - Off
/User/CF/No_Answer/.body: Forwards incoming calls to another number when the user does not answer within the number of rings set on this page. When it is on, it takes precedence over sending unanswered calls to voice mail, so turn it off if missed calls should go to the user's mailbox.

/User/CF/Not_Reachable/.title: Call Forwarding Not Reachable - Off
/User/CF/Not_Reachable/.body: Forwards incoming calls to another number when the user's phone cannot be reached, for example when it is unregistered or has lost its network connection. It keeps calls flowing during an outage at the customer's site, typically by sending them to a mobile or another office.

/User/Icn/.title: Call Notify - Off
/User/Icn/.body: Sends a notification to an email address the user chooses when an incoming call matches criteria the user sets, such as specific callers or a time schedule. The call itself is handled as usual; Call Notify only adds the alert.

/User/COLR/.title: Connected Line Identification Restriction - Off
/User/COLR/.body: Stops the user's identity from being presented back to the caller when the user answers a call. The caller's phone then cannot show who actually picked up, which matters when calls reach the user through forwarding, pickup or a hunt group.

/User/DND/.title: Do Not Disturb - Off
/User/DND/.body: Sends all incoming calls to the user's busy treatment instead of ringing the phone, which normally means voice mail if the user has it, otherwise a busy signal. An optional ring reminder plays a short ring on the phone when a call is diverted, so the user knows calls are arriving.

/User/ExternalCLIDDelivery/.title: External Calling Line ID Delivery - On
/User/ExternalCLIDDelivery/.body: Controls whether the user sees the caller's name and number on calls from outside the group or enterprise. Callers who block their identity stay withheld either way, and calls from inside the group or enterprise are controlled by Internal Calling Line ID Delivery.

/User/InternalCLIDDelivery/.title: Internal Calling Line ID Delivery - On
/User/InternalCLIDDelivery/.body: Controls whether the user sees the caller's name and number on calls from other users in the same group or enterprise. Calls from outside are controlled separately by External Calling Line ID Delivery, so the two can be set differently.

/User/SilentAlerting/.title: Silent Alerting - Off
/User/SilentAlerting/.body: Presents incoming calls to the user's phone without an audible ring, so the user can see a call arrive and choose to answer it without disturbing others. It relies on the phone honoring the silent alert signal from BroadWorks, so check that the phone model supports it.

/User/AutomaticHoldRetrieve/.title: Automatic Hold/Retrieve - Off
/User/AutomaticHoldRetrieve/.body: Makes this user act as a hold position: a call transferred to its number is automatically put on hold, and anyone who dials the number picks up the waiting call. A recall timer set on the page sends a held call back if nobody retrieves it in time.

/User/AlternateNumbers/.title: Alternate Numbers
/User/AlternateNumbers/.body: Gives the user extra phone numbers or extensions that all ring the same user, each of which can have its own distinctive ring so the user can tell which number was called. The numbers must be assigned to the group before they can be added here.

/User/SCF/.title: Call Forwarding Selective - Off
/User/SCF/.body: Forwards incoming calls that match criteria the user sets, such as specific callers, a time schedule or holidays, to a chosen number. Calls that don't match are handled as usual, and a matching call is forwarded by this service even when Call Forwarding Always is also on.

/User/CallMeNow/.title: Call Me Now - Off
/User/CallMeNow/.body: Lets someone request a call with the user, typically through a web page or application: BroadWorks first calls the requester's number and then connects them to the user. Settings on the page control whether the requester must confirm before being connected, and criteria that limit which requests are accepted.

/User/CommPilot_Express/.title: CommPilot Express - Off
/User/CommPilot_Express/.body: Lets the user switch between preset profiles (Available In Office, Available Out Of Office, Busy and Unavailable), each with its own rules for incoming calls, such as forwarding, voice mail and email notification. Choosing a profile applies all of its call handling at once instead of changing each service separately.

/User/CustomRingback/.title: Custom Ringback User - Off
/User/CustomRingback/.body: Plays a chosen audio or video file to callers in place of the normal ringing tone while they wait for the user to answer. Different files can be used for different criteria, such as specific callers or a time schedule, and calls that match no criteria hear normal ringback.

/User/ExternalCustomRingback/.title: External Custom Ringback - Off
/User/ExternalCustomRingback/.body: Plays ringback to the user's callers from an external ringback server instead of the normal ringing tone, for example music supplied by a third-party service. It depends on such a server being set up for the system, and the page controls whether and how the user's calls use it.

/User/PersonalAssistant/.title: Personal Assistant - Off
/User/PersonalAssistant/.body: Lets the user set an away status, such as Out of Office, Meeting or Vacation, with an optional end time. While it is set, callers hear an announcement about the user's absence and can be offered a transfer to an attendant number or to voice mail.

/User/PreAlertingAnnouncement/.title: Pre-alerting Announcement - Off
/User/PreAlertingAnnouncement/.body: Plays an announcement to callers before the user's phone starts ringing, such as a notice that calls may be recorded. The page sets the audio or video file to play and the criteria that decide which incoming calls hear it.

/User/PRCW/.title: Priority Alert - Off
/User/PRCW/.body: Gives incoming calls that match criteria the user sets, such as specific callers or a time schedule, a distinctive ring so the user can recognize important calls. Other calls ring normally, and the distinctive ring only sounds on phones that support it.

/User/SCA/.title: Selective Acceptance - Off
/User/SCA/.body: Lets through only incoming calls that match criteria the user sets, such as specific numbers or a time schedule. Callers who don't match hear an announcement that the user is not accepting calls, which suits users who should only be reachable by a known list of people.

/User/SCR/.title: Selective Rejection - Off
/User/SCR/.body: Rejects incoming calls that match criteria the user sets, such as specific numbers, anonymous callers or a time schedule, and plays those callers an announcement that the user is not accepting calls. Calls that don't match reach the user as usual.

/User/SeqRing/.title: Sequential Ring - Off
/User/SeqRing/.body: Rings a list of the user's other numbers one after another, such as a mobile and then a home phone, so a call can find the user. Each number has its own ring count, criteria decide which calls use the service, and if nobody answers the call follows the user's no-answer handling, such as voice mail.

/User/SimRing/Family/.title: Simultaneous Ring Family - Off
/User/SimRing/Family/.body: Rings a list of other numbers, such as other household members' phones, at the same time as the user's own phone, and the first phone answered takes the call. It works like Simultaneous Ring Personal but is assigned as a separate service, so check which one the user actually has.

/User/SimRing/.title: Simultaneous Ring Personal - Off
/User/SimRing/.body: Rings the user's phone and a list of other numbers, such as a mobile, at the same time and connects the call to whichever answers first. Answer confirmation can be required on the other numbers, so a call is not lost to a mobile's voice mail.

/User/TerminatingAlternateTrunkIdentity/.title: Terminating Alternate Trunk Identity
/User/TerminatingAlternateTrunkIdentity/.body: Sets an alternate identity that BroadWorks sends to the PBX when delivering incoming calls for this user over a trunk group, in place of the user's usual identity. It applies only to trunking setups where the PBX needs a specific identity to route the call to the right place.

/User/AutomaticCallback/.title: Automatic Callback - Off
/User/AutomaticCallback/.body: Lets the user ask to be called back when a number they dialed was busy. BroadWorks watches that line and, once it is free, rings the user and then connects the call to the other party, which saves the user from redialing a colleague who is on the phone.

/User/Classmark/.title: Classmark
/User/Classmark/.body: Assigns this user one of the classmarks defined by the system operator, a tag that BroadWorks carries on the user's calls so other network elements can give them different treatment. Change it only when the carrier's or the customer's setup specifically calls for a classmark on this user.

/User/CallReturn/.title: Call Return
/User/CallReturn/.body: Lets the user call back the last person who called them by dialing a feature access code, whether or not that call was answered. BroadWorks keeps track of the last caller's number for the user, so it works from any of the user's phones.

/User/CPC/.title: Calling Party Category
/User/CPC/.body: Sets the calling party category sent with the user's outgoing calls, which tells the network what type of line is calling, such as an ordinary line or a payphone. Carriers can use it for routing, billing or call restrictions, so change it only when the line really is a special type.

/User/LegacyAutomaticCallback/.title: Legacy Automatic Callback - On
/User/LegacyAutomaticCallback/.body: The callback-on-busy feature in the form used with legacy telephone networks: the user can ask to be called back when a busy number they dialed becomes free, and BroadWorks then connects the call. It is a separate service from Automatic Callback, so check which one the user has before troubleshooting.

/User/LNR/.title: Last Number Redial
/User/LNR/.body: Lets the user redial the last number they called from their line by dialing a feature access code. BroadWorks remembers that number on the network side, so it works even on phones that have no redial key of their own.

/User/CIDB/.title: Line ID Blocking - Off
/User/CIDB/.body: Hides the user's number and name from the people the user calls, on every outgoing call. It is a standing setting, and a separate per-call service can let the user show or hide their identity on individual calls when needed.

/User/ResourcePriority/.title: Resource Priority
/User/ResourcePriority/.body: Sets the resource priority value BroadWorks signals on the user's outgoing calls, which networks that support it use to give those calls priority handling, for example for government or emergency staff. Change it only when the customer is entitled to priority service on the carrier's network.

/User/SC8/.title: Speed Dial 8
/User/SC8/.body: Lets the user store up to eight frequently called numbers on single-digit speed codes and call each one by dialing its short code from their phone. Entries can be set on this page or by the user from the phone with a feature access code.

/User/SC100/.title: Speed Dial 100
/User/SC100/.body: Lets the user store up to 100 frequently called numbers on two-digit speed codes and call each one by dialing its code. Each entry can have a description, which makes a long list easier to manage, and it suits users with many regular contacts.

/User/NumberPortabilityAnnouncement/.title: Number Portability Announcement - Off
/User/NumberPortabilityAnnouncement/.body: Plays the user a short announcement before connecting a call to a number that has been ported to another network, so the user knows the number is now served by a different operator. The call then continues as normal after the announcement.

/User/Phone_List/Personal/.title: Personal Phone List
/User/Phone_List/Personal/.body: Holds the user's own list of names and numbers, which the user can browse and call from supported phones and clients. Entries here are private to the user, unlike the group and enterprise common phone lists that everyone in the group or enterprise shares.

/User/PreferredCarrierUser/.title: Preferred Carrier User
/User/PreferredCarrierUser/.body: Chooses the long distance carriers used for the user's intra-LATA, inter-LATA and international calls, overriding the group's preferred carrier setting. Leave it on the group setting unless this user must use a different carrier from the rest of the group.

/User/TSD/.title: Two-Stage Dialing - On
/User/TSD/.body: Lets the user call in from another phone, such as a mobile, reach BroadWorks and then dial a second number so the call is placed as if from the user's business line. The outgoing call then follows the user's own calling restrictions and services rather than the mobile's.

/User/BargeinExempt/.title: Barge-in Exempt - On
/User/BargeinExempt/.body: Protects the user's active calls from being joined by other users, such as through Directed Call Pickup with Barge-in. It is useful for staff who handle confidential calls, and it does not stop others from picking up calls still ringing on the user's phone.

/User/CW/.title: Call Waiting - On
/User/CW/.body: Lets the user receive a second call while already on one: the user hears a tone and can answer the new call, putting the first on hold. With it off, a second caller gets the user's busy treatment, such as Call Forwarding Busy or voice mail.

/User/CustomerOriginatedTrace/.title: Customer Originated Trace
/User/CustomerOriginatedTrace/.body: Lets the user flag a harassing or malicious call right after it ends by dialing a feature access code. BroadWorks then records the details of that last incoming call for the service operator to follow up, without revealing the caller's identity to the user.

/User/DirectedCallPickup/.title: Directed Call Pickup
/User/DirectedCallPickup/.body: Lets the user answer a call ringing on another user's phone by dialing a feature access code followed by that user's extension or number. Unlike Call Pickup, it works without both users belonging to the same pickup group.

/User/DiversionInhibitor/.title: Diversion Inhibitor
/User/DiversionInhibitor/.body: Marks calls from the user, or calls the user redirects, so the destination does not forward them on, for example to its own voice mail. This helps when a call must reach a person, such as a forwarded call that should not end up in a mobile's voice mailbox.

/User/DPUBI/.title: Directed Call Pickup with Barge-in
/User/DPUBI/.body: Lets the user answer a call ringing at another user's phone by dialing a feature access code plus that user's extension. If the call has already been answered, the user can barge in and join it as a three-way call. The page sets whether a warning tone plays when the user barges in.

/User/FlashCH/.title: Flash Call Hold
/User/FlashCH/.body: Lets the user put an active call on hold from a phone that signals with hook flash, such as an analog line on an adapter, and later return to the held call. It is mainly useful on devices that have no hold button of their own.

/User/CallTransfer/.title: Call Transfer
/User/CallTransfer/.body: Lets the user transfer an active call to another number, either blind without speaking first or after consulting the recipient. The page also sets Call Transfer Recall, which returns an unanswered blind transfer to the user after a number of rings, and whether a transfer to a busy line can camp on and wait.

/User/ICSA/.title: In-Call Service Activation - Off
/User/ICSA/.body: Lets the user reach mid-call services such as transfer or conference by pressing a digit sequence on the keypad instead of using hook flash. It is useful when the user answers on a device that cannot flash, such as a mobile or other phone reached through BroadWorks Anywhere or Remote Office.

/User/ThreeWayCall/.title: Three-Way Call
/User/ThreeWayCall/.body: Lets the user add one more party to an active call, forming a three-way conference: the first call is put on hold, the second party is dialed, and the calls are joined. For conferences with more than three people in total, the user needs N-Way Call instead.

/User/MOHUser/.title: Music/Video On Hold - On
/User/MOHUser/.body: Plays music or video to callers the user places on hold, instead of silence. The source normally comes from the group's Music On Hold settings, and this page lets the user's calls opt out or, where the group allows it, use the user's own audio or video file.

/User/PreferredAnswerEndpoint/.title: Preferred Answer Endpoint
/User/PreferredAnswerEndpoint/.body: Sets which of the user's devices, such as the primary phone or a shared call appearance, is preferred for answering calls when the answer is triggered remotely, for example from a desktop or receptionist client. It is useful when the user has several registered endpoints and wants those calls to connect on one specific device.

/User/NWayCall/.title: N-Way Call
/User/NWayCall/.body: Lets the user build an ad hoc conference from their phone, adding several other parties to the same call one at a time. Assign it to users who regularly pull more than one colleague or outside caller into a call; Three-Way Call covers only a single extra party.

/User/CallRecording/.title: Call Recording - Off
/User/CallRecording/.body: Sends the user's calls to the recording platform the provider has connected to BroadWorks. The page sets when calls are recorded, from Never through Always to On Demand, where the user chooses during the call to keep a recording, and whether the parties hear an announcement or tone that recording is in progress.

/User/CommunicationBarring/.title: Communication Barring User-Control
/User/CommunicationBarring/.body: Lets the user switch between Communication Barring profiles that an administrator has made available, for example to lock the phone against outgoing calls when away from the desk. The user changes profile with a personal PIN, and this page shows the available profiles and which one is currently active.

/User/AdviceOfCharge/.title: Advice of Charge
/User/AdviceOfCharge/.body: Sends charge information for the user's calls to their device, either during the call or at its end, depending on the setting on this page. It is only useful when the phone or client can display charges and the provider supplies the charging data.

/User/BroadWorksAnywhere/.title: BroadWorks Anywhere
/User/BroadWorksAnywhere/.body: Lets the user make and receive business calls on other phones, such as a mobile or home line, as if using their desk phone. Each added location can ring alongside the user's main device, and Require Answer Confirmation stops a call from being taken by that phone's own voice mail.

/User/BroadWorksMobility/.title: BroadWorks Mobility - Off
/User/BroadWorksMobility/.body: Ties a mobile number on the provider's mobile network to the user's BroadWorks profile, so business calls can ring the mobile and calls made from it use the user's business services. The page sets which phones ring, such as the fixed phone, the mobile or both.

/User/Call_Center/.title: Call Centers
/User/Call_Center/.body: Shows the call centers the user belongs to as an agent and whether the user has joined each one to take its calls. The page also sets the user's ACD state, such as Available or Unavailable, which decides whether call center calls are offered to the user.

/User/ChargeNumber/.title: Charge Number
/User/ChargeNumber/.body: Assigns a separate charge number to the user, which is used for billing instead of the user's own number and can be sent toward the network on the user's calls. It is typically used when calls from several users or a virtual user should be billed against one main number.

/User/Executive/.title: Executive
/User/Executive/.body: Lets the user work with one or more assistants who can answer, screen and place calls on the user's behalf. The page lists the assigned assistants and sets call filtering, which decides which incoming calls go to the assistants, and screening, which alerts the user to calls the assistants are handling.

/User/ExecutiveAssistant/.title: Executive-Assistant
/User/ExecutiveAssistant/.body: Lets the user act as an assistant to one or more executives, answering and placing calls on an executive's behalf. The page shows which executives the user supports and whether the user has opted in to each, and it can divert the executives' calls to another number when the assistant is away.

/User/FlexibleSeatingGuest/.title: Flexible Seating Guest - Off
/User/FlexibleSeatingGuest/.body: Lets the user sign in to a shared phone set up as a flexible seating host, so that phone takes on the user's number and settings while the user sits there. The page turns the service on, shows the host in use and can limit how long an association lasts.

/User/GroupNightForwarding/.title: Group Night Forwarding - Off
/User/GroupNightForwarding/.body: Sends calls for the user to the group's night destination when the group has night forwarding switched on or its after-hours or holiday schedule applies. The group administrator sets the destination and schedules, and this page decides whether the user follows the group setting or keeps receiving calls as normal.

/User/HotelingGuest/.title: Hoteling Guest - Off
/User/HotelingGuest/.body: Lets the user link their profile to a hoteling host phone, so the user's number and services follow them to that desk for the length of the association. The page turns the service on, selects the host and sets whether the association ends after a time limit.

/User/HotelingHost/.title: Hoteling Host - Off
/User/HotelingHost/.body: Makes this user's phone available as a shared hotel desk that guests can temporarily take over with their own profile. The page turns hosting on, can enforce a time limit on guest associations, and sets whether guests can come from this group only or from the whole enterprise.

/User/MEED/.title: Mobile Extension to Extension Dialing
/User/MEED/.body: Lets the user reach colleagues by dialing their extension from a mobile phone, the same way they would from a desk phone. It applies to the user's mobile calls that BroadWorks handles, such as through BroadWorks Mobility, so short extension numbers are recognized instead of being treated as ordinary mobile dialing.

/User/PBXIntegration/.title: PBX Integration
/User/PBXIntegration/.body: Lets this user profile represent a customer's PBX, so calls to the user's numbers are delivered to the PBX, which then routes them to its own extensions. It is an alternative to connecting the PBX through a trunk group.

/User/PTT/.title: Push to Talk
/User/PTT/.body: Lets the user make intercom-style calls that the other phone answers automatically on speaker, for quick announcements or two-way talk. The page sets whether incoming push-to-talk calls are auto-answered, whether connections are one-way or two-way, and which users are allowed or blocked from reaching this user.

/User/PhysicalLocation/.title: Physical Location - Off
/User/PhysicalLocation/.body: Lets BroadWorks take account of the user's physical location, as reported by the network or device, for services that depend on where the user is calling from. Turn it on only when the provider uses location information, for example for location-based calling restrictions.

/User/RemoteOffice/.title: Remote Office - Off
/User/RemoteOffice/.body: Lets the user treat another phone, such as a home or hotel line, as their business phone. When it is on, incoming calls ring the remote number instead of the user's main device, and calls placed from a desktop client can go out through that phone with the user's business identity.

/User/SCAP/.title: Shared Call Appearance
/User/SCAP/.body: Lets the user's line appear on additional devices, such as a second desk phone or a softphone, which ring alongside the primary phone. The page lists these extra endpoints and sets options such as whether other appearances can bridge into an active call and whether a call can be retrieved from another appearance.

/User/VideoAddOn/.title: Video Add-On - Off
/User/VideoAddOn/.body: Lets the user pair an audio-only phone with a separate video-capable endpoint, so calls can carry video to that endpoint while audio stays on the phone. The page turns the service on and identifies the video endpoint.

/User/ZoneCallingRestrictions/.title: Zone Calling Restrictions
/User/ZoneCallingRestrictions/.body: Limits where the user can use their service by comparing the device's IP address with the user's home zone, a set of address ranges defined by the provider. Calls from a device outside the home zone can be blocked or handled differently, and the page sets which zone is home.

/User/Calling_Plan/Incoming/.title: Incoming Calling Plan
/User/Calling_Plan/Incoming/.body: Controls which incoming calls reach the user, such as calls from outside the group or collect calls. The page either follows the group's default incoming calling plan or applies custom settings to this user only.

/User/Calling_Plan/Outgoing/?isEnh=true.title: Outgoing Calling Plan
/User/Calling_Plan/Outgoing/?isEnh=true.body: Controls which call types the user can dial, such as local, toll, international or premium numbers, and whether a blocked call is refused, needs an authorization code or is transferred. The page uses the group's default plan or custom settings for this user, with separate settings for calls the user forwards or transfers.

/User/Calling_Plan/OutgoingAuthCodes/?is.title: Outgoing Authorization Codes
/User/Calling_Plan/OutgoingAuthCodes/?is.body: Lists the authorization codes accepted when the user's outgoing calling plan requires a code for a call type, such as international calls. The codes can come from the group or be set for this user only, and the code entered is recorded against the call.

/User/Calling_Plan/OutgoingDigitPlan/?is.title: Outgoing Digit Plan
/User/Calling_Plan/OutgoingDigitPlan/?is.body: Applies outgoing call rules to specific digit patterns defined by the group, rather than to broad call types. For each pattern the page sets whether the user may originate, forward or transfer calls to matching numbers, following the group's default or custom settings for this user.

/User/Calling_Plan/OutgoingPinholeDigitP.title: Outgoing Pinhole Digit Plan
/User/Calling_Plan/OutgoingPinholeDigitP.body: Makes exceptions to the user's outgoing restrictions for specific digit patterns, so chosen numbers stay reachable even when their call type is blocked. For example, a user barred from toll calls can still be allowed one approved number, and the page follows the group's default or uses custom settings.

/User/Calling_Plan/TransferNumbers/?isEn.title: Transfer Numbers
/User/Calling_Plan/TransferNumbers/?isEn.body: Sets the first, second and third transfer numbers that blocked calls are sent to when a calling plan rule says to transfer rather than simply disallow. A common use is routing restricted calls to an operator or reception desk.

/User/BusyLampField/.title: Busy Lamp Field
/User/BusyLampField/.body: Lets the user's phone or client show whether monitored colleagues are idle, ringing or on a call. The page holds the list of users to monitor and the list URI that the device subscribes to, so the phone must also be set up with that URI.

/User/OfficeCommunicatorTab/.title: Office Communicator Tab
/User/OfficeCommunicatorTab/.body: Licenses the BroadWorks tab for Microsoft Office Communicator, which lets the user see and control their BroadWorks calls and settings from within that client. It has no effect unless the user runs Office Communicator with the tab installed.

/User/BroadWorksAgent/.title: BroadWorks Agent
/User/BroadWorksAgent/.body: Licenses the BroadWorks call center agent client, a desktop application for handling call center calls and changing the agent's ACD state. Assign it to users who work as agents in a call center; which call centers they belong to is set separately.

/User/BroadWorksSupervisor/.title: BroadWorks Supervisor
/User/BroadWorksSupervisor/.body: Licenses the BroadWorks call center supervisor client, which lets the user monitor agents and queues and follow their activity. Assign it to users who supervise call center agents; the agents each supervisor can see are set in the call center's own settings.

/User/ClientLicense4/.title: BroadWorks Receptionist - Enterprise
/User/ClientLicense4/.body: Licenses the Enterprise edition of the Receptionist client, a desktop console for attendants who handle calls for many colleagues. The receptionist sees monitored users' call status and can answer, transfer and hold calls for them, and this page sets which users are monitored.

/User/ReceptionistSmallBusiness/.title: BroadWorks Receptionist - Small Business
/User/ReceptionistSmallBusiness/.body: Licenses the Small Business edition of the Receptionist client, a desktop console for a front desk that answers and routes calls for colleagues. The receptionist sees whether monitored users are busy before transferring a call, and this page sets which users are monitored.

/User/ReceptionistOffice/.title: BroadWorks Receptionist - Office
/User/ReceptionistOffice/.body: Licenses the Office edition of the Receptionist client, a desktop console for someone who answers and passes on calls for a small team. The receptionist can see whether monitored colleagues are on the phone before transferring, and this page sets which users are monitored.

/User/PolycomPhoneServices/.title: Polycom Phone Services
/User/PolycomPhoneServices/.body: Connects the user's Polycom phone directory to BroadWorks, so the phone can show the group or enterprise directory. The page sets whether the directory is integrated and whether the user's personal phone list and a group custom contact directory are included.

/User/VM/Aliases/.title: Aliases
/User/VM/Aliases/.body: Lists additional phone numbers that also lead to this voice mailbox, so messages left or sent to those numbers arrive in the same mailbox. It is useful when callers still use an older or secondary number to reach the user.

/User/VM/DistList/?list=0.title: Distribution Lists
/User/VM/DistList/?list=0.body: Holds the user's voice messaging distribution lists, which let the user send one voice message to several people at once from the voice portal. Each list has a number and a description, and its members are the phone numbers or extensions that receive the message.

/User/VM/Greetings/.title: Greetings
/User/VM/Greetings/.body: Sets what callers hear when they reach the user's voice mailbox, including the busy and no-answer greetings and the recorded personal name. It also sets how many rings pass before an unanswered call goes to voice mail.

/User/IntegratedIMP/.title: Integrated IM&P - Off
/User/IntegratedIMP/.body: Turns on the provider's integrated instant messaging and presence service for the user, so supported BroadWorks clients can show presence and exchange chat messages under the user's business identity. It only has an effect where the provider has an IM&P server connected to BroadWorks.

/User/ShortMessageService/.title: Short Message Service
/User/ShortMessageService/.body: Allows the user to send and receive text messages through BroadWorks on their business identity, for use with supported clients or mobile services. It depends on the provider having text messaging set up, so assigning the service on its own may not enable texting.

/User/VM/General/.title: Voice Management - Off
/User/VM/General/.body: Sets up the user's voice mailbox: whether voice messaging is on, whether new messages stay in the mailbox or are forwarded to an email address, and which calls go to voice mail, such as busy or unanswered calls. It also covers email notification of new messages and the message waiting light on the phone.

/User/VoicePortal/.title: Voice Portal
/User/VoicePortal/.body: Sets up access to the voice portal, the phone menu used to check messages, record greetings and change some call settings. Access is protected by the voice portal passcode, and the settings here apply to this user or virtual user only.

/User/FaxMessaging/.title: Fax Messaging - Off
/User/FaxMessaging/.body: Gives the user a fax number whose incoming faxes are received by BroadWorks and delivered as messages, for example by email, according to the mailbox settings. Turn it on for users who need to receive faxes without a fax machine; the page sets the fax number and extension.

/User/MWIMobile/.title: MWI Delivery to Mobile Endpoint - Off
/User/MWIMobile/.body: Sends a new voice message notification for the user's BroadWorks mailbox to their mobile phone, so the mobile shows when messages are waiting. It is used together with BroadWorks Mobility, and the provider sets up how the notification is delivered.

/User/VM/OutgoingMWI/.title: Outgoing MWI
/User/VM/OutgoingMWI/.body: Sends message waiting indication for this mailbox to other phone numbers, typically phones on a PBX or legacy system reached through an SMDI link, so they show when new messages arrive. The page turns it on and lists the numbers that receive the indication.

/User/ThirdPartyMWI/.title: Third-Party MWI Control
/User/ThirdPartyMWI/.body: Lets an outside voice mail system turn the user's message waiting light on and off through BroadWorks, for users whose messages are kept on that system rather than on BroadWorks. It is normally paired with Third-Party Voice Mail Support.

/User/ExternalVoiceMail/.title: Third-Party Voice Mail Support - Off
/User/ExternalVoiceMail/.body: Sends the user's calls to an external voice mail system instead of BroadWorks voice messaging, always, when busy or when unanswered after a set number of rings. The page sets those conditions and which mailbox and voice mail server are used.

/User/VoicePortalCalling/.title: Voice Portal Calling - On
/User/VoicePortalCalling/.body: Lets the user place outgoing calls from within the voice portal, for example after dialing in from a hotel or mobile phone. The call is presented with the user's business number rather than the number of the phone they dialed in from.

/User/Authentication/.title: Authentication
/User/Authentication/.body: Holds the SIP authentication user name and password the user's device must present when it registers or places calls. They must match what is configured on the phone, so changing them here without updating the device will stop it registering.

/User/BasicCallLogs/.title: Basic Call Logs
/User/BasicCallLogs/.body: Shows the user's recent placed, received and missed calls, with the number, name and time of each. It is a quick way to check whether a call reached the user, but the list keeps only a limited number of entries of each type.

/User/DeviceActivation/.title: Device Activation
/User/DeviceActivation/.body: Manages activation codes for the user's devices, so a phone or client can be claimed and provisioned for this user by entering a short code instead of typing a MAC address or credentials. The code rules, such as length and expiry, come from the device onboarding policy.

/User/EnhancedCallLogs/.title: Enhanced Call Logs
/User/EnhancedCallLogs/.body: Keeps a larger, more detailed history of the user's placed, received and missed calls than Basic Call Logs, and the history can be searched and filtered. It suits users, or administrators troubleshooting for them, who need to look further back in time.

/User/Feature_Codes/.title: Feature Access Codes
/User/Feature_Codes/.body: Lists the feature access codes available to the user, the short codes dialed from the phone to use services such as forwarding or Do Not Disturb. The codes shown depend on the services assigned and the group's code settings, so the page is a quick reference when helping a customer.

/User/CompanyDir/.title: Group Directory
/User/CompanyDir/.body: Shows the directory of the user's group, listing colleagues with their phone numbers and extensions. The page is read-only and searchable, making it a quick way to look up a number while working in the user's profile.

/User/MobileAppRegistrations/.title: Mobile App Registrations
/User/MobileAppRegistrations/.body: Shows the mobile client applications registered for this user, such as a softphone app on a smartphone or tablet. It helps confirm whether the user's mobile app has signed in, for example when calls are not reaching it.

/Intercept/?id=user.title: Intercept User - Off
/Intercept/?id=user.body: Stops normal calling for the user without removing the profile, for example while a line is suspended or a number has moved. Incoming callers hear an announcement and can be told a new number or sent elsewhere, and outgoing calls can be blocked or limited.

/User/Prepaid/.title: Prepaid - Off
/User/Prepaid/.body: Puts the user's calls under prepaid charging, where an external charging system checks for available credit and can stop calls when the balance runs out. It only works where the provider has connected such a charging system to BroadWorks.

/User/PushNotification/.title: Push Notification
/User/PushNotification/.body: Lets BroadWorks wake the user's mobile client app with a push notification when a call arrives, so the app can ring even while it is in the background. It is used for mobile softphone clients that rely on push rather than staying connected.

/User/PushNotificationRegistrations/.title: Push Notification Registrations
/User/PushNotificationRegistrations/.body: Lists the mobile apps and devices that have registered with BroadWorks to receive push notifications for this user, with details of each registration. It is useful when checking why a user's mobile app is not ringing for incoming calls.

/User/Registrations/.title: Registrations
/User/Registrations/.body: Shows the devices currently registered for the user, with each device's contact address, expiry time and line port. It is the first place to check when a user's phone is not ringing or cannot make calls, since a missing registration means BroadWorks cannot reach that device.

/User/SecurityClassification/.title: Security Classification - On
/User/SecurityClassification/.body: Assigns the user a security classification level, mostly used in government or defense settings. During a call BroadWorks works out the classification that all parties share and can announce it, so participants know the level of information they may discuss.

/Group/Auto_Attendant/Modify/.title: Profile
/Group/Auto_Attendant/Modify/.body: Sets this Auto Attendant's main details: its name, calling line ID, language and time zone, plus the business hours and holiday schedules and the scope for extension and name dialing. The schedules chosen here decide whether callers hear the business hours, after hours or holiday menu, so check them first when callers reach the wrong greeting.

/Group/Auto_Attendant/Addresses/.title: Addresses
/Group/Auto_Attendant/Addresses/.body: Sets the phone number, extension and any alias addresses callers can use to reach this Auto Attendant. A phone number must already be assigned to the group before it can be chosen here, and an Auto Attendant with only an extension can still be reached internally.

/Group/Auto_Attendant/Submenus/.title: Submenus
/Group/Auto_Attendant/Submenus/.body: Creates and edits this Auto Attendant's submenus, each with its own greeting and keypad actions. Callers reach a submenu when a key on one of the main menus or on another submenu is set to transfer to it, which lets you build layered choices such as separate sales and support options.

/Group/Auto_Attendant/MenuBusinessHours/.title: Business Hours Menu
/Group/Auto_Attendant/MenuBusinessHours/.body: Sets the greeting and keypad options callers get during business hours, such as transferring to an operator or extension, dialing by name or extension, or repeating the menu. Business hours come from the schedule chosen on the Profile page; at other times the After Hours Menu or Holiday Menu plays instead.

/Group/Auto_Attendant/MenuAfterHours/.title: After Hours Menu
/Group/Auto_Attendant/MenuAfterHours/.body: Sets the greeting and keypad options callers get outside business hours, meaning any time not covered by the business hours schedule on the Profile page. Check that its keys do not send callers to phones nobody answers at night, and note that if no business hours schedule is chosen, this menu never plays.

/Group/Auto_Attendant/MenuHoliday/.title: Holiday Menu
/Group/Auto_Attendant/MenuHoliday/.body: Sets the greeting and keypad options callers get on the dates in the holiday schedule chosen on the Profile page. On those dates it takes priority over both the business hours and after hours menus, which makes it the place for an office-closed greeting.

/Group/Hunt_Group/Modify/.title: Profile
/Group/Hunt_Group/Modify/.body: Sets this Hunt Group's name, calling line ID, time zone, members and group policy, plus the no-answer rules for moving on or forwarding the call. The policy decides who rings: Regular always starts at the top of the list, Circular starts after whoever took the last call, Simultaneous rings everyone and Uniform picks whoever has been idle longest.

/Group/Hunt_Group/Addresses/.title: Addresses
/Group/Hunt_Group/Addresses/.body: Sets the phone number, extension and any alias addresses that callers dial to reach this Hunt Group. Calls to any of these addresses are offered to the group's members according to the policy on the Profile page, and a phone number must be assigned to the group before it can be picked here.

/User/PrivacyServiceInstance/.title: Privacy
/User/PrivacyServiceInstance/.body: Sets privacy options for this Hunt Group or Call Center, such as leaving it out of the group and enterprise directory and stopping Auto Attendant callers from reaching it by name or extension dialing. These settings only hide it from those lookups; anyone who knows the number or extension can still call it directly.

/User/DirectoryNumberHunting/.title: Directory Number Hunting
/User/DirectoryNumberHunting/.body: Chooses which members of this Hunt Group or Call Center have calls to their own direct numbers hunt through the group, so a call to a busy or unanswered member can be taken by someone else. Options set whether the call rings that member first and whether the member's own busy and no-answer handling applies if nobody picks up.

/User/SmdiMessageDesk/.title: SMDI Message Desk - Off
/User/SmdiMessageDesk/.body: Sets up SMDI Message Desk for this Hunt Group, which sends call details such as the calling number and the reason the call was redirected to an external voice mail system over an SMDI link. It is only needed when the customer's voice mail runs on a separate platform; the On or Off in the menu shows its current state.

/Group/Call_Center/AddModify/.title: Profile
/Group/Call_Center/AddModify/.body: Sets this Call Center's name, calling line ID, time zone, queue length and group policy, along with queue options such as letting callers press an escape digit to leave the queue. The group policy decides which available agent gets the next call, for example whoever has been idle longest under Uniform, or every agent at once under Simultaneous.

/Group/Call_Center/Addresses/.title: Addresses
/Group/Call_Center/Addresses/.body: Sets the phone number, extension and any alias addresses callers dial to reach this Call Center. Calls to any of these addresses enter the queue and are offered to agents according to the policy on the Profile page, and a phone number must be assigned to the group before it can be picked here.

/Group/Call_Center/Agents/.title: Agents
/Group/Call_Center/Agents/.body: Assigns the users who take calls for this Call Center and shows whether each one has joined it. Only users with a Call Center service assigned to them can be added, and under the Regular and Circular policies the order of agents in this list sets the order in which they are offered calls.

/User/CCStatistics/.title: Status & Statistics
/User/CCStatistics/.body: Shows the current status of this Call Center's queue and agents along with its call statistics, such as calls received, answered and abandoned. It is a quick first check when a customer reports long waits or missed calls, before you look at the routing policies or agent settings.

/Group/Call_Center/Supervisors/.title: Supervisors
/Group/Call_Center/Supervisors/.body: Assigns the users who supervise this Call Center, which lets them follow its queue and agents from a supervisor client. Being a supervisor does not put someone in the call queue, so a supervisor only receives queued calls if they are also added on the Agents page.

/Group/Call_Center/Thresholds/.title: Thresholds
/Group/Call_Center/Thresholds/.body: Sets warning levels for this Call Center's queue, such as the number of calls waiting, the longest current wait, the average speed of answer and the number of abandoned calls. When a value crosses its threshold, agent and supervisor clients can show an alert, and a notification email can also be sent to the address set here.

/User/Announcements/Entrance/.title: Announcements
/User/Announcements/Entrance/.body: Sets the audio callers hear while waiting in this Call Center's queue, such as the entrance message, comfort messages and music on hold. It also covers the whisper message, which plays only to the agent before the call connects so they know which Call Center the call came from.

/Group/Call_Center/RoutingPolicies/Disti.title: Distinctive Ringing
/Group/Call_Center/RoutingPolicies/Disti.body: Sets whether agents' phones use a distinctive ring pattern for calls delivered from this Call Center, so agents can tell queue calls apart from calls to their own numbers. The chosen ring pattern only makes a difference on phones that support distinctive ringing.

/Group/Call_Center/RoutingPolicies/Bounc.title: Bounced Calls
/Group/Call_Center/RoutingPolicies/Bounc.body: Decides what happens when an agent is offered a call from this Call Center and does not answer within the set number of rings: the call is taken back and offered to another agent. It can also make the agent who missed the call unavailable, so the queue stops sending calls to someone who has stepped away.

/Group/Call_Center/RoutingPolicies/Overf.title: Overflow
/Group/Call_Center/RoutingPolicies/Overf.body: Decides what happens to calls when this Call Center's queue is full, or when a call has waited longer than the time allowed. Calls can get busy treatment, be transferred to another number or keep hearing ringing until the caller hangs up, and an announcement can play before the overflow action.

/Group/Call_Center/RoutingPolicies/Stran.title: Stranded Calls
/Group/Call_Center/RoutingPolicies/Stran.body: Decides what happens to calls waiting in this Call Center's queue when no agents are left to answer them, for example because every agent has signed out or left the Call Center. Options include keeping calls in the queue, giving them busy treatment or transferring them to another number, so they are not left waiting indefinitely.

/Group/Call_Center/RoutingPolicies/Stran.title: Stranded Calls - Unavailable
/Group/Call_Center/RoutingPolicies/Stran.body: Decides what happens to calls waiting in this Call Center's queue when all of its agents are set to Unavailable, so nobody is taking calls even though agents are still signed in. It is separate from Stranded Calls, which covers agents who have signed out, so review both pages together.

Profile.title: Profile
Profile.body: The Profile menu groups the core identity and administration options for this level — service providers/enterprises, groups, users, service instances, administrators, and the reseller's own profile. It's the default landing area for day-to-day provisioning.

Resources.title: Resources
Resources.body: The Resources menu manages the building blocks consumed by groups and users — numbers, identity/device profiles and endpoints, domains, device management tag sets, and number ranges. This is where you provision the inventory that services are later assigned from.

Services.title: Services
Services.body: The Services menu is where calling features and service packs are configured and assigned at this level — the telephony capabilities (call forwarding, voicemail, etc.) that get authorized and applied to users and groups.

Call Center.title: Call Center
Call Center.body: The Call Center menu manages BroadWorks Call Center (ACD) resources — queues, agents, supervisors, routing policies, and reporting. Use it to configure inbound contact-center behavior such as skill/priority routing and agent availability.

Meet-Me Conferencing.title: Meet-Me Conferencing
Meet-Me Conferencing.body: Meet-Me Conferencing manages dial-in audio conference bridges — conference ports, host/attendee access codes, and scheduling. Use it to provision the bridges that let multiple participants dial a common number to join a call.

Utilities.title: Utilities
Utilities.body: The Utilities menu collects administrative and diagnostic tools at this level — bulk operations, inventory reports, and lookups that assist with managing the reseller's groups, users, and resources at scale.

Communication Barring.title: Communication Barring
Communication Barring.body: The Communication Barring menu holds the barring rules this service provider's groups can use. Digit Pattern Criteria group dialed-digit patterns under a name, and Profiles combine criteria and call types into rules that allow or block the calls users make, forward and receive.

Meet-Me Conferencing.title: Meet-Me Conferencing
Meet-Me Conferencing.body: The Meet-Me Conferencing menu manages conference capacity for this service provider. Meet-Me Conference Ports shows how many ports it has to share among its groups, and each port carries one conference participant at a time.

Profile.title: Profile
Profile.body: The Profile menu covers this service provider's identity and everything under it. It lists its groups, users and service instances, manages administrators and schedules, and sets provider-wide policies and options such as call processing, dial plan, alternate user IDs, device onboarding, routing profile and dialable caller ID.

Resources.title: Resources
Resources.body: The Resources menu manages what this service provider makes available to its groups — numbers, domains, services, identity/device profiles and endpoints, network classes of service, carriers, office zones and enterprise trunk number ranges and prefixes. Groups can only use what has been authorized or assigned here.

Services.title: Services
Services.body: The Services menu sets provider-wide options for services used across its groups, such as voice messaging, Voice Portal, BroadWorks Mobility, In-Call Service Activation, advice of charge, number portability query and third-party emergency calling. Changes here generally reach every group under this service provider.

Utilities.title: Utilities
Utilities.body: The Utilities menu holds provider-wide rules and tools — password, passcode, SIP and device authentication password rules, feature access codes, emergency call notification, device configuration and event queues, Voice Portal branding and service pack migration. Groups can follow many of these rules or set their own.

Acct/Auth Codes.title: Acct/Auth Codes
Acct/Auth Codes.body: The Acct/Auth Codes menu sets up codes users enter on outgoing calls. Administration chooses account codes, which tag calls for tracking, or authorization codes, which must be valid for the call to proceed, plus the code length and which users need one. Codes Management keeps the list of codes.

Call Center.title: Call Center
Call Center.body: The Call Center menu manages the group's call centers and the settings they share. Beyond the call center list, it holds agent defaults, threshold profiles, unavailable and disposition codes, routing priority, call center monitoring, and reporting setup such as templates, branding, scheduled reports and external reporting.

Calling Plan.title: Calling Plan
Calling Plan.body: The Calling Plan menu sets group-wide rules for the calls users can receive, make and transfer. Incoming and Outgoing Calling Plans allow or block call types, digit plans cover specific dialed strings, and authorization codes and transfer numbers handle calls that need a code or are redirected. Users follow these unless given their own.

Communication Barring.title: Communication Barring
Communication Barring.body: The Communication Barring menu chooses which of the service provider's barring profiles this group may use and which one applies by default. The profile in force decides which calls the group's users can make, forward and receive.

Meet-Me Conferencing.title: Meet-Me Conferencing
Meet-Me Conferencing.body: The Meet-Me Conferencing menu sets up dial-in conferencing for this group. Meet-Me Conference Ports shows how many ports the group can use, and Meet-Me Conference Bridges creates the bridges participants dial into, each with its own number, port allowance and assigned conference hosts.

Profile.title: Profile
Profile.body: The Profile menu covers the group's identity and structure — its profile details, users, departments, administrators, schedules and announcement repository. It also holds group policies for call processing, dial plan, web portal access and device onboarding, plus alternate user IDs and communication barring authorization codes.

Resources.title: Resources
Resources.body: The Resources menu shows what this group has to work with — its numbers, domains, authorized services, identity/device profiles and endpoints, network classes of service, office zones, call recording platform and enterprise trunk number ranges. Numbers and services must reach the group from the service provider before users can be given them.

Services.title: Services
Services.body: The Services menu sets up group-wide services — virtual users such as auto attendants, hunt groups and VoiceXML, plus shared features like call park, call pickup, music/video on hold, voice messaging, Voice Portal and Exchange integration. These are configured once for the group rather than per user.

Utilities.title: Utilities
Utilities.body: The Utilities menu gathers group-wide tools — the group directory, common phone list, custom contact directories, inventory report, feature access codes, extension dialing length, password and passcode rules, emergency call notification and device configuration. Use it to review what the group holds and adjust rules shared by its users.

Call Control.title: Call Control
Call Control.body: The Call Control menu holds services that shape how calls are handled once connected, such as call waiting, call transfer, three-way calling, flash hold, directed call pickup, barge-in exemption, music/video on hold and call recording. Where an entry shows On or Off, that is the service's current state.

Calling Plans.title: Calling Plans
Calling Plans.body: The Calling Plans menu controls which calls this user, auto attendant, hunt group or call center can receive, make and transfer. Incoming and Outgoing Calling Plans allow or block call types, digit plans cover specific dialed strings, and authorization codes and transfer numbers handle calls that need a code or are redirected.

Client Applications.title: Client Applications
Client Applications.body: The Client Applications menu configures client software and phone applications linked to this user, such as BroadWorks Receptionist, Agent and Supervisor, Busy Lamp Field, Polycom Phone Services and the Office Communicator tab. Only clients whose services are assigned to the user appear here.

Incoming Calls.title: Incoming Calls
Incoming Calls.body: The Incoming Calls menu holds services that decide how calls to this user, auto attendant, hunt group or call center are handled — forwarding, Do Not Disturb, anonymous rejection, caller name and number delivery, alternate numbers, call notify and Call Me Now. Where an entry shows On or Off, that is its current state.

Messaging.title: Messaging
Messaging.body: The Messaging menu covers voice mail and related services — voice management, greetings, aliases, distribution lists, fax messaging, Voice Portal access, message waiting indicators, SMS and third-party voice mail support. Where an entry shows On or Off, that is its current state for this user, hunt group or call center.

Outgoing Calls.title: Outgoing Calls
Outgoing Calls.body: The Outgoing Calls menu holds services that affect the calls this user places, such as speed dial, last number redial, call return, automatic callback, line ID blocking, personal phone list and resource priority. Where an entry shows On or Off, that is the service's current state.

Profile.title: Profile
Profile.body: The Profile menu holds the core setup of this user, auto attendant, hunt group or call center — name and addresses, passwords, announcement repository, assigned services and call policies. Virtual users add their own entries here, such as auto attendant submenus and a call center's agents, supervisors, thresholds and announcements.

Utilities.title: Utilities
Utilities.body: The Utilities menu gathers tools for this user's devices and records, such as call logs, feature access codes, the group directory, device activation, SIP authentication, registrations and push notification settings. It also lists services like Intercept User and Prepaid, where On or Off shows whether they are active.

Menus.title: Menus
Menus.body: The Menus section sets what callers hear and which keys they can press on this auto attendant. The Business Hours, After Hours and Holiday menus each have their own greeting and key options, and the auto attendant picks one using its business hours and holiday schedules.

Routing Policies.title: Routing Policies
Routing Policies.body: The Routing Policies menu decides what this call center does with calls it cannot handle normally. Bounced Calls covers calls an agent does not answer, Overflow covers calls that wait too long or find the queue full, and the Stranded Calls pages cover calls left when no agents are signed in or all are unavailable.

Reseller ID.title: Reseller ID
Reseller ID.body: The unique identifier for this reseller in BroadWorks, used to link its service providers and enterprises to it. It is an administrative key only and has no effect on how calls are routed or handled.

Name.title: Name
Name.body: The reseller's descriptive name, shown to administrators in lists and search results. Changing it only affects how the reseller appears in the portal; it does not change the Reseller ID, its service providers or any calls.

Call Forwarding Always.title: Call Forwarding Always
Call Forwarding Always.body: When On, every incoming call to this user is forwarded straight to the number or SIP-URI below, and the user's own phones do not ring. When Off, calls are delivered normally and the user's other forwarding and voice mail settings apply.

Calls Forward to phone number / SIP-URI.title: Calls Forward to phone number / SIP-URI
Calls Forward to phone number / SIP-URI.body: The destination that receives all of this user's calls while Call Forwarding Always is On, such as a home office or mobile number, an extension or a SIP-URI. It must be a destination the user's outgoing calling plan permits.

Play Ring Reminder when a call is forwar.title: Play Ring Reminder when a call is forwarded
Play Ring Reminder when a call is forwar.body: When checked, the user's primary phone gives a short ring burst each time a call is forwarded, as a reminder that Call Forwarding Always is on. The call is still forwarded; when unchecked, calls are forwarded silently.

Do Not Disturb.title: Do Not Disturb
Do Not Disturb.body: When On, incoming calls do not ring the user's phones and are sent straight to voice mail, or given the user's busy treatment if there is no voice mail. When Off, calls ring normally.

Play Ring Reminder when a call is blocke.title: Play Ring Reminder when a call is blocked
Play Ring Reminder when a call is blocke.body: When checked, the user's primary phone gives a short ring burst each time Do Not Disturb sends a call away, as a reminder the service is on. The call is still not answered at the phone; when unchecked, calls are blocked silently.

Anonymous Call Rejection.title: Anonymous Call Rejection
Anonymous Call Rejection.body: When On, calls from callers who deliberately hide their number are rejected and the caller is told the user does not accept calls from unidentified callers. Callers whose number is simply unavailable, and calls from within the group, still ring. When Off, anonymous calls ring normally.

Enable External Calling Name Delivery.title: Enable External Calling Name Delivery
Enable External Calling Name Delivery.body: When On, the user's phone shows the caller's name on calls from outside the group or enterprise, when one is provided. When Off, external callers' names are not shown. This setting also controls seeing the answering party's name on external calls the user places.

Enable Internal Calling Name Delivery.title: Enable Internal Calling Name Delivery
Enable Internal Calling Name Delivery.body: When On, the user's phone shows the caller's name on calls from inside the group or enterprise. When Off, internal callers' names are not shown. This setting also controls seeing the answering party's name on internal calls the user places.

Enable External Calling Number Delivery.title: Enable External Calling Number Delivery
Enable External Calling Number Delivery.body: When On, the user's phone shows the caller's number on calls from outside the group or enterprise, unless the caller has blocked it. When Off, external callers' numbers are not shown. This setting also controls seeing the answering party's number on external calls the user places.

Enable Internal Calling Number Delivery.title: Enable Internal Calling Number Delivery
Enable Internal Calling Number Delivery.body: When On, the user's phone shows the number or extension of callers inside the group or enterprise. When Off, internal callers' numbers are not shown. This setting also controls seeing the answering party's number on internal calls the user places.

Automatic Hold/Retrieve.title: Automatic Hold/Retrieve
Automatic Hold/Retrieve.body: When On, incoming calls to this user are held and retrieved automatically, giving an alternate way to hold and pick up calls without using feature access codes. When Off, calls to this user are handled normally.

Automatically retrieve the call after.title: Automatically retrieve the call after
Automatically retrieve the call after.body: The number of seconds a call can stay on automatic hold before BroadWorks retrieves it automatically. A shorter time brings held callers back sooner, so they are not left waiting unnoticed.

Call Me Now.title: Call Me Now
Call Me Now.body: When On, a caller can use a Call Me Now web link to enter their own phone number; BroadWorks calls that number first and, once answered, places the call to this user. When Off, Call Me Now requests are not accepted.

Answer Confirmation.title: Answer Confirmation
Answer Confirmation.body: Sets what the requesting party must do after answering the Call Me Now call, before BroadWorks calls this user. None connects at once, Any Key requires a key press, and Passcode requires a passcode, so a voice mailbox answering does not complete the call.

MWI Delivery to Mobile Endpoint.title: MWI Delivery to Mobile Endpoint
MWI Delivery to Mobile Endpoint.body: When On, BroadWorks notifies the user's mobile phone when a new voice mail, fax or video message arrives, by SMS or message waiting indication if the phone supports it. When Off, no mobile notification is sent.

Mobile Phone Number.title: Mobile Phone Number
Mobile Phone Number.body: The mobile phone number that receives new-message notifications while MWI Delivery to Mobile Endpoint is On. Enter the user's own mobile number; the phone needs SMS or message waiting indication support to show the alert.

Send Missed Call Alert when no Voice Mai.title: Send Missed Call Alert when no Voice Mail is deposited
Send Missed Call Alert when no Voice Mai.body: When checked, the mobile phone also gets an alert when a call to the user is missed and the caller leaves no voice mail. When unchecked, notifications are sent only for new messages.

Call Forwarding Always Secondary.title: Call Forwarding Always Secondary
Call Forwarding Always Secondary.body: When On, all incoming calls to this user are forwarded to the secondary number or SIP-URI below instead of ringing the user's phones. It works like Call Forwarding Always but keeps its own destination. When Off, it does not forward calls.

Calls Forward to phone number / SIP-URI.title: Calls Forward to phone number / SIP-URI
Calls Forward to phone number / SIP-URI.body: The secondary destination that receives all of this user's calls while Call Forwarding Always Secondary is On. Enter a phone number, extension or SIP-URI; it must be a destination the user's outgoing calling plan permits.

Play Ring Reminder when a call is forwar.title: Play Ring Reminder when a call is forwarded
Play Ring Reminder when a call is forwar.body: When checked, the user's primary phone gives a short ring burst each time a call is forwarded to the secondary destination, as a reminder the service is on. The call is still forwarded; when unchecked, calls are forwarded silently.

Call Forwarding No Answer.title: Call Forwarding No Answer
Call Forwarding No Answer.body: When On, calls the user does not answer are forwarded to the number or SIP-URI below after the set number of rings, instead of going to voice mail. When Off, unanswered calls follow the user's other no-answer handling, such as voice mail.

Calls Forward to phone number / SIP-URI.title: Calls Forward to phone number / SIP-URI
Calls Forward to phone number / SIP-URI.body: The destination that receives calls the user does not answer while Call Forwarding No Answer is On, such as a co-worker, assistant or mobile number, or a SIP-URI. It must be a destination the user's outgoing calling plan permits.

Number of rings before forwarding.title: Number of rings before forwarding
Number of rings before forwarding.body: How many times the user's phone rings before an unanswered call is forwarded. A lower number sends callers on sooner; a higher number gives the user more time to pick up before the call leaves their phone.

Two-Stage Dialing.title: Two-Stage Dialing
Two-Stage Dialing.body: When On, calls the user places from an associated mobile phone or landline to their own BroadWorks number are answered with a prompt for more digits. The digits entered are then dialed as if from the user's BroadWorks phone. When Off, no prompt is played.

Allow activation with any user address.title: Allow activation with any user address
Allow activation with any user address.body: When checked, calling any of the user's own phone numbers, extensions or aliases from an associated phone triggers the prompt for more digits. When unchecked, dialing those addresses is not treated as a Two-Stage Dialing request.

Call Waiting.title: Call Waiting
Call Waiting.body: When On, the user hears a call waiting tone when a second call arrives during a call and can switch to it. When Off, the second caller gets the user's busy treatment, such as voice mail or Call Forwarding Busy.

Disable Calling Line ID Delivery on Call.title: Disable Calling Line ID Delivery on Call Waiting
Disable Calling Line ID Delivery on Call.body: When checked, the user's phone does not show the waiting caller's name or number during a call waiting alert; only the tone is heard. When unchecked, the waiting caller's identity is shown if the phone supports it.
